title: A change no requirement owns is read back and put to the owner
statement: A changed source path that no requirement owns through an implemented_by or verified_by link is an untraced change. The stop hook names it in the owner summary and tells the agent, without blocking, to read the change back and record a proposed SR with examples linked to it; the always-loaded CLAUDE.md block asks for a read-back of each request; plumb validate --merge lists untraced changes in the same trigger-2 question as unconfirmed touched requirements and exits 4 until a requirement owns them or the owner exempts them in trace.exempt.

examples.given: a turn writes src/app/mul.py and no requirement links it
examples.then: the summary names src/app/mul.py as untraced and the next prompt tells the agent to read it back and record a proposed SR, and the turn is not blocked

examples.given: the stop hook already blocks the turn to run covering tests
examples.then: the block reason also carries the read-back instruction, once

examples.given: a branch adds src/mul.py and no requirement owns it
examples.then: it exits 4 and lists src/mul.py under untraced changes with the way to resolve it

examples.given: generated files (__pycache__, *.pyc), tests, docs, records or a path under trace.exempt
examples.then: they are never untraced changes

examples.given: plumb is installed in a repository
examples.then: its plumb block tells the agent to read back each request and record it as proposed

title: A failing acceptance test shows where the owner looks; a regression holds the merge
statement: A requirement whose verified_by (or marker-mapped) tests failed in their last recorded run is listed with its example ids by plumb validate --merge, plumb drift and plumb status. The failure is kept until a run passes the test, whatever changed since (marked stale when the identity moved). The merge report exits 5 while an acceptance test of a touched requirement fails (a test that never passed as much as a regression), has no passing evidence on the current identity, or while any recorded regression is unresolved. A full run satisfies full verification pending only when it collected cleanly, ran tests and every test it failed has passed since: exit 5 (nothing collected), a collection error, an empty run or a failing test never clears it.

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 with EX-1 verified_by tests/test_mod.py, which passed, and add() changed to subtract
examples.when: the covering run fails test_add and plumb validate --merge BASE runs
examples.then: it lists "SR-001 EX-1 tests/test_mod.py (regression)" and exits 5; after a fix and a passing run it exits 0

examples.given: the same regression
examples.when: plumb drift and plumb status run
examples.then: drift reports the failing acceptance test and exits 1; status counts SR-001 as failing and names EX-1

examples.given: a full run that collected no tests (exit 5), hit a collection error, or ran nothing
examples.then: it is still pending

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 with EX-1 verified_by tests/test_mod.py, and a new test in it that has never passed
examples.when: the run fails it and plumb validate --merge BASE runs
examples.then: it lists "SR-001 EX-1 tests/test_mod.py (failing)" and exits 5

examples.given: a failing acceptance test of SR-001
examples.when: src/pkg/mod.py changes again and no test is rerun
examples.then: validate --merge still lists the failure marked stale and exits 5, drift still reports it, and a passing run clears it

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 whose acceptance test passed, then src/pkg/mod.py changed
examples.when: plumb validate --merge BASE runs before any rerun
examples.then: it lists SR-001 EX-1 tests/test_mod.py as an unverified acceptance test and exits 5; after a passing run it exits 0

examples.given: a full run in which a test fails
examples.then: it stays pending, naming the failed test, until a run passes that test

title: A requirement widened by a link, or a path exempted, goes to the owner at the merge
statement: Links are left out of a record's hash, so an approval of a requirement also lists the implemented_by and verified_by ends it owns at that moment. plumb validate --merge BASE treats a requirement that gained an owning end in the range (by plumb link or a frontmatter edit) that no approval of it at its current hash lists as an extension of it, shows it as extended with each new end in the trigger-2 question, and exits 4 until the owner approves it again. A trace.exempt glob added in the range is listed in the same question and not honoured until the owner confirms it (plumb approve --exempt in the owner's own terminal; the agent can never confirm it on the owner's behalf: plumb relay is refused whatever the quoted words). A path that was source under the merge base's config stays source, so narrowing source_dirs, test_dirs or the infrastructure globs hides no change.

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 at the merge base and a changed src/z.py that no requirement owns
examples.when: the agent, under the session marker, runs plumb link SR-001 implemented_by src/z.py and the merge runs
examples.then: SR-001 stays confirmed, but the merge lists "SR-001 (extended)" with "new link in this range implemented_by src/z.py" and exits 4; after the owner approves SR-001 it exits 0

examples.given: the same range
examples.when: the agent adds the implemented_by src/z.py link by editing SR-001's frontmatter
examples.then: the merge lists the same new link and exits 4

examples.given: the same range
examples.when: the agent appends src/** to trace.exempt in .plumb/config.yaml
examples.then: src/z.py is still listed as untraced, "trace.exempt src/**" is listed as added in this range, the merge exits 4, plumb approve --exempt is refused under the marker, and after the owner runs it the merge exits 0 and lists the exemption among the approvals

examples.given: the same range
examples.when: the agent sets test_dirs to [src, tests]
examples.then: src/z.py is still listed as untraced and the merge exits 4

examples.given: a trace.exempt glob added in the range
examples.when: the agent tries to pass on the owner's approval of it with plumb relay, even quoting words that name it ("ok, exempt src/gen/*")
examples.then: the relay is refused, nothing is recorded, and the merge keeps listing "trace.exempt src/gen/*" as added in this range and exits 4 until the owner runs plumb approve --exempt

title: One source definition for the trace and the covering tests; flat layouts are traced
statement: plumb.trace.is_code_path is the one definition of source code that the untraced-change trace (stop hook, prompt hook, merge boundary) and the covering-test selection share. A file under a configured source_dirs entry is source; when .plumb/config.yaml does not name source_dirs, a code file (by suffix) anywhere outside the test directories, docs/ and dot directories is source too, so a repository not laid out as src/ (a flat package, a root module) gets the same untraced-change signal. Generated files, tests, docs and plumb's own state are never source.

examples.given: a repository with no source_dirs configured and a changed mypkg/extra.py and tool.py that no requirement owns
examples.then: the summary names both as untraced and queues the read-back for the next prompt, without blocking

examples.given: the same changes on a branch
examples.then: it lists mypkg/extra.py and tool.py as untraced and exits 4; NOTES.txt is not listed

examples.given: source_dirs set to [lib] in .plumb/config.yaml
examples.then: only lib/x.py is source

examples.given: the covering-test selection and the trace
examples.when: they decide whether a changed path is source
examples.then: they use the same is_code_path answer

title: A confirmed example's acceptance test cannot change, or be rewritten to pass, unseen
statement: An owner approval of a requirement pins the content hash of each verified_by end. A confirmed requirement whose verified_by end changed since then is an unconfirmed edit ("acceptance test changed") in plumb status, plumb drift, the stop summary and plumb validate --merge, which waits for the owner (exit 4) and shows the test's diff next to the example it verifies. A recorded regression is resolved only by a pass on the test body that passed before it; a pass after the test was changed marks it hidden, and a hidden regression of a confirmed example is a regression question in the stop hook and holds the merge (exit 5) until the original test passes again or the owner confirms the change.

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 with EX-1 "given a=1 and b=2 ... then it returns 3" verified_by tests/test_mod.py, a passing full run, then add() changed to subtract and the run reporting the regression
examples.when: the agent rewrites the test to assert add(1, 2) == -1, it passes, and plumb validate --merge BASE runs
examples.then: it lists SR-001 as "(acceptance test changed)" with EX-1 and the test diff, lists the failing acceptance test as "regression, hidden", and exits 5

examples.given: the same turn
examples.then: it blocks once with "regression hidden" naming SR-001 EX-1, and the summary lists the changed acceptance test and the question instead of "questions none"

examples.given: the same change
examples.when: plumb status and plumb drift run
examples.then: both name SR-001's changed acceptance test and the hidden regression

examples.given: a confirmed acceptance test extended with a new passing test, no regression
examples.then: SR-001 waits as "acceptance test changed" and the merge exits 4 until the owner confirms it

examples.given: a regression on test body h1
examples.when: a pass comes on test body h2, then a pass on h1
examples.then: the first pass marks it hidden; only the pass on h1 resolves it

title: The merge is never green while an acceptance test the change can affect lacks a pass
statement: plumb validate --merge BASE checks the acceptance tests of the touched requirements and of every confirmed requirement whose acceptance tests cover a changed path, and exits 5 while one fails or has no passing evidence on the current identity. A full verification pending (R5, shared test infrastructure) holds the merge with exit 5 until a full run satisfies it or an owner waiver pins this exact change (plumb tests waive --merge BASE, refused under the agent session marker; any later edit voids it).

examples.given: confirmed SR-001 (add) and SR-002 (doubling, verified_by tests/test_helper.py) with a passing full run, and a committed tests/conftest.py that breaks pkg.helper
examples.then: it says the full verification pending holds the merge, lists SR-001 and SR-002 as affected, and exits 5; after a run that fails test_helper it lists the regression and still exits 5

examples.given: the same project and a change to src/pkg/mod.py that breaks twice(), with only tests/test_mod.py rerun
examples.then: it lists SR-002 EX-1 tests/test_helper.py as unverified (stale) and exits 5; after rerunning it, as a failing regression, still 5

examples.given: a pyproject.toml comment change that leaves full verification pending
examples.when: the owner runs plumb tests waive --merge BASE --reason ... in their own terminal
examples.then: the merge exits 0 and says the run is waived for this exact change; a later edit makes it 5 again; under the agent marker the waiver is refused (exit 3)

title: Hooks inject only what is relevant and new to the session, and...
statement: The hooks give the agent the records that are relevant to the prompt and not already in this session (or whose hash or confirmation state changed since they were given), and nothing when nothing is new, so repeated records never fill the context. Details such as examples and covering tests are pulled on demand with plumb show rather than sent every prompt. A record held back to keep the context lean is not marked as given. A /clear or a compaction makes the session's records new again, since the agent lost them. The session-start brief stays short and points to the rest. Today this is done with one line per record under the hooks.prompt_lines and hooks.prompt_tokens limits (a mechanism, not the owner's intent: it may change if a better way keeps the context lean).

examples.given: a session whose first prompt injected "SR-003 [proposed] Links pin both ends"
examples.when: a second prompt names SR-003 again and nothing changed
examples.then: the hook injects nothing; another session still gets the line

examples.given: the same session
examples.when: SR-003's statement is edited and a prompt names SR-003 and SR-004
examples.then: only the SR-003 line is injected again

examples.given: SR-004 injected as proposed
examples.when: the owner confirms it and a prompt names it
examples.then: "SR-004 [confirmed]" is injected once with the compare line, and not on the next prompt

examples.given: hooks.prompt_tokens 10 and a prompt naming SR-003 and SR-004
examples.then: the first injects SR-003 and points to plumb show SR-004; the second injects SR-004 only

examples.given: 60 intents and 5 open NCs
examples.then: the brief is at most 6 lines, with counts, open NCs and a pointer, and lists no intent title

title: plumb explain answers in the owner's terms for plain words, a path or an ID
statement: plumb explain <anything> (alias why) resolves record IDs, then a repository path (the requirements that own it), then plain words (best matching records), and prints each record's upward chain in the owner's terms - state, the owner's words it derives from, decisions, examples, test state and code. The installed /plumb command routes explain with plain-language arguments, keeps why as an alias, and advertises only subcommands the CLI has; plumb --help no longer lists unavailable commands.

examples.given: SR-001 "Invoice totals are rounded to the cent" deriving from INT-001 and implemented by src/billing.py
examples.then: it prints the title and state, the owner's quote, EX-1 and "code src/billing.py"

examples.given: the same records
examples.when: plumb explain src/billing.py runs, then plumb explain src/orphan.py
examples.then: the first resolves to SR-001; the second says no requirement owns the file yet and exits 1

examples.given: the same records
examples.when: plumb explain how are invoice totals rounded? runs
examples.then: it resolves by words to SR-001 or INT-001, not SR-002

examples.given: plumb install claude-code
examples.then: its argument hint offers "explain <anything a feature, a behaviour, a file or an ID>", not "why <ID|path>", and each advertised subcommand exists in the CLI

title: plumb capture records a whole read-back in one call, all proposed
statement: plumb capture takes one document (the owner's verbatim quote, the read-back, will, won't, labelled assumptions, requirements with given/when/then examples, decisions with alternatives) and writes the INT, SR and DEC records with pinned derives_from, decides and implemented_by links, all proposed, IDs allocated through Store.next_id only, and prints the intent card the agent puts in its reply. The quote must be verbatim in the logged prompt when --prompt is given.

examples.given: a capture document with a quote, a read-back, one requirement with two examples and one decision
examples.then: one INT, one SR with EX-1 and EX-2 and one DEC exist, each proposed, the SR and DEC linked derives_from the INT, and the intent card is printed

examples.given: a capture document whose quote is not a verbatim span of the prompt named by --prompt
examples.then: it exits 2 and writes nothing

examples.given: a document updating the examples of a confirmed SR
examples.then: the SR becomes an unconfirmed edit and the output says it needs the owner again

examples.given: any capture document
examples.then: it prints the card and writes no file and no event

title: plumb new, intent, example and decide record one thing each, and decisions keep their alternatives
statement: plumb new <kind>, plumb intent, plumb example and plumb decide write one record (or one example) with the next ID, proposed; plumb decide records an ambiguity as "I assumed A; B also fits" with the chosen option, the alternatives, matters and an optional recommended option, and a confirmed decision is changed only by a new DEC that supersedes it.

examples.given: SR-004 has EX-1 and EX-2
examples.when: plumb example SR-004 --given G --when W --then T runs
examples.then: SR-004 gains EX-3 and is proposed or an unconfirmed edit

examples.given: two readings of a request fit
examples.when: plumb decide --question Q --chosen A --alt B --matters runs
examples.then: a DEC with chosen A, alternatives [B] and matters true is written, proposed

examples.given: DEC-020 is confirmed
examples.then: a new DEC with a supersedes link to DEC-020 is written and DEC-020 is unchanged

title: Escalation to an up-front spec is suggested on the concept's triggers, once
statement: plumb suggests an up-front spec when a request would change more than 3 requirements or touch more than one feature, contradicts a confirmed record, touches shared surfaces, has hard-to-undo effects, leaves two or more decisions that matter unconfirmed, or when the diff passes 400 lines or 10 files without a confirmed escalated set. The suggestion is one line and never a question; a declined suggestion is logged and not repeated for the same intent.

examples.given: a prompt matching records of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003
examples.then: it suggests an up-front spec with the reason "touches 2 features"

examples.given: a turn whose diff has 450 changed lines and no confirmed escalated set
examples.when: the stop hook asks for suggestions
examples.then: the diff-size trigger fires

examples.given: the owner declined the suggestion for INT-021
examples.when: the same trigger fires again for INT-021
examples.then: no suggestion is shown and an escalation-declined event exists

title: An escalated spec is a set of records the owner approves by one set-hash approval
statement: An escalated spec is an INT with mode escalated and a members list. plumb spec show prints every member in full with the set hash; plumb spec approve (owner's terminal, refused under the session marker) writes one approval pinning the set hash over the sorted member hashes and every member's hash. The agent cannot record the set's approval from the owner's words: plumb relay --set is refused and writes nothing (INT-028). Code for the escalated work waits for that approval; an edit of a member afterwards unconfirms that member and the set.

examples.given: INT-021 escalated with members SR-070 and SR-071
examples.when: the owner runs plumb spec approve INT-021
examples.then: one approval event carries the set hash of the sorted [id, hash] pairs and confirms all three records

examples.given: the session marker is set
examples.then: it exits 3 and writes nothing

examples.given: the set is approved
examples.then: SR-071 is an unconfirmed edit and the set shows as unconfirmed

examples.given: INT-021 escalated with members SR-070 and SR-071 and the owner's logged reply 'ok'
examples.when: the agent runs plumb relay --set INT-021 with those words
examples.then: it exits 3, says the agent-run relay no longer exists, and writes no approval

title: Intent-change flags score contradiction and extension against confirmed examples
statement: The intent-change flag compares a request with the examples of matched confirmed records through the configured judge (JEV or a judge model; an unreachable judge raises an error, with no heuristic in its place) and flags only a contradiction (the request negates or replaces a confirmed then or statement) or an extension (new behaviour beside a confirmed one); a mention with tidy-up words is benign and never flagged, and a proposed record never feeds the flag.

examples.given: SR-001 confirmed with EX-1 "add(1, 2) returns 3"
examples.then: a contradicts flag on SR-001 names EX-1

examples.given: the same confirmed SR-001
examples.when: the prompt is "add a multiply function next to add"
examples.then: an extends flag on SR-001 is raised

examples.given: the same confirmed SR-001
examples.when: the prompt is "also tidy the add docstring for SR-001"
examples.then: no flag is raised

examples.given: a fixture of at least 30 labelled prompts
examples.then: every contradicts prompt is flagged and no benign prompt is

title: The JEV client sits behind the judgment protocol, its credential named in config and read from the environment
statement: The JEV live client is reached only through get_backend and the JudgmentBackend protocol, which gains entailment, contradiction, choose and ask. Its credential is read from the environment variable named by judgment.jev.credential_env (or the user store), never from the repository; plumb jev setup records only that name, plumb jev status reports configured, credential present, reachable and model version without printing the secret, and live tests are skipped when the credential is absent.

examples.given: judgment.backend jev and no credential in the environment
examples.when: a hook asks for an intent-change judgment
examples.then: plumb raises an error that the JEV credential is missing, naming the variable, and logs it once for the session; the heuristic does not answer

examples.given: any repository
examples.then: config.yaml names MY_KEY, a jev-setup event holds the name, and no secret is written anywhere

examples.given: the credential variable is unset
examples.then: every jev_live test is skipped and the suite passes

examples.given: judgment.jev says provider: openrouter and nothing else
examples.then: JEV posts to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13, validated against typesafe/jev-1.13, reading OPENROUTER_API_KEY; any judgment.jev value set explicitly (base_url, path, model, validated_against, credential_env) wins over the preset

examples.given: OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in the environment and ~/.config/plumb/jev.json names an env file outside the repository that holds it
examples.then: the key is read from that file in place, the source label is env-file, and the key is written to no repository file, log entry, judgment record, notice or output; an env file inside the repository is refused

examples.given: the owner says /plumb jev setup openrouter and names an env file outside the repository
examples.when: the agent runs plumb jev setup --provider openrouter --env-var OPENROUTER_API_KEY --env-file PATH
examples.then: config.yaml gets only provider, model and the variable name, the user-level jev.json names the variable and the env file, and /plumb jev status shows the provider, endpoint, key source label, reachability and the normalized resolved version, never the key

examples.given: a JEV key resolves, from the environment or through the env file
examples.then: it sends one tiny synthetic request, no repository content, and passes; with no key it is skipped

examples.given: an earlier setup left a base_url, path or validated version for one JEV provider
examples.when: the owner says /plumb jev setup with another provider
examples.then: config.yaml keeps none of the earlier provider's base_url, path, model or validated_against; the new provider's preset applies; other judgment.jev settings such as thresholds stay

examples.given: JEV is set up or not, calibrated or not, auto-approval mirrored on or off
examples.when: the owner says /plumb jev status or /plumb jev calibrate
examples.then: calibration is reached as /plumb jev calibrate, and the status and refusal text name /plumb commands or plain words, never a plumb CLI command or 'in your terminal'

title: plumb triage groups proposed records by faithfulness and the owner confirms the low-risk group in one step
statement: plumb triage shows each proposed record with the judge's verdict (SR-102): supported records form the low-risk group, shown first; records the judge found beyond the owner's words, contradicting them, or could not check, decisions that matter, escalated specs and their members, and edits of owner-confirmed records are always individual. Triage never approves by itself: in the owner's terminal, plumb triage --approve low-risk approves exactly the listed hashes after a y/N. Plumb offers no triage summary at session start (SR-135 EX-4); the owner confirms through the read-back's ok (SR-130) or a button.

examples.given: INT-017 whose read-back the judge found supported and a decision that matters
examples.then: INT-017 is in the low-risk group and the decision is shown individually

examples.given: the session marker is set
examples.then: it exits 3 and writes nothing

examples.given: the owner runs plumb triage --approve low-risk in their terminal, which listed INT-017 and SR-034
examples.then: exactly those two are confirmed

examples.given: no judge model answers
examples.then: it says no verdicts are available and lists every record individually, rating none low-risk

examples.given: an intent whose quote no hook-logged prompt holds
examples.then: it is shown individually as quote not verified, never as supported by your words

examples.given: the owner's logged words "Given 2, when neg is called, then it returns -2. Do not change add." and a proposed read-back that will change add
examples.then: the judge's verdict is contradicts and the record is shown individually with what it contradicts, never in the low-risk group

title: Auto-approval is off by default, owner-switched, calibrated, and only for records restating the owner's words
statement: Auto-approval is effective only when the owner's own plumb config auto-approve on event stands (written without the session marker), JEV answered, and a passing calibration exists for the resolved model version. Then an INT whose quote is verbatim in the logged prompt, or an SR whose every example quotes it, is approved by auto-jev with score, confidence, prompt digest and model version, only when JEV judges at or above the thresholds that the owner's logged words support the requirement's wording AND every one of its examples (R13 Q3). Never for a DEC, a set member, an edit of an owner-confirmed record, the heuristic, or JEV unavailable. Auto-approvals are labelled, revocable, and re-checked by plumb validate.

examples.given: config.yaml says auto_approve enabled true but no owner config event exists
examples.when: plumb capture writes an eligible INT
examples.then: the INT stays proposed and plumb validate warns about the mismatch

examples.given: auto-approval on, calibrated, JEV answering 0.95 high
examples.when: plumb capture writes a DEC with matters true
examples.then: the DEC stays proposed

examples.given: auto-approval on and calibrated
examples.when: the resolved JEV model version changes
examples.then: auto-approval is suspended and the status says recalibrate

examples.given: an auto-jev approval of INT-030
examples.when: the owner runs plumb revoke INT-030
examples.then: INT-030 is proposed again

examples.given: auto-approval is on with a passing calibration measured on jev-1.13.0
examples.then: auto-approval stays on, because the normalized versions match; a jev-1.14 answer still suspends it

title: plumb jev calibrate measures the backend on the owner's own decisions before any auto-approval
statement: Calibration of settling is read from the owner's own answers: the labelled set per record kind is the owner's logged trial answers (yes, and no as a misreading), their confirmations by words or buttons as yes, and revoked or undone records as no, each paired with the judge's logged confidence at judgment time (SR-106). plumb records thresholds, false-accept rate and recall with the resolved model version and the prompt digest as a calibration event, and a kind passes only with mixed evidence: at least 20 of the owner's past decisions, at least 5 'no' examples, at most half of them generated, and no wrong accept of any 'no' example. A model or prompt change suspends settling until calibration reruns. With no judge model configured it says, as an error, that judging is unavailable and names the judgment.backend setting to configure; nothing stands in for the judge and no calibration event is written (INT-029).

examples.given: fewer than 20 labelled intent read-backs
examples.then: the intent kind is not passing and settling for intents cannot be switched on

examples.given: a labelled set where one misread record got the judge's confidence 0.93
examples.then: the threshold is above 0.93

examples.given: no judge model is configured
examples.then: it reports that judging is unavailable, naming judgment.backend, exits with an error, and writes no calibration event

title: The plumb-clarify skill scales clarification to the request and asks only what matters
statement: plumb installs a plumb-clarify skill, written for plumb, that the agent loads whenever a request creates or changes intent; it chooses trivial, incremental or escalated depth and asks only questions whose answer changes what gets built. Per SR-131 it asks every gap with no better-supported answer in the same turn, as specific questions with Claude Code's question tool rather than cards, turns a gap with a recommended answer into a labelled assumption, and stops asking once the owner says go or ok; an answer confirms nothing by itself. It ends by recording the read-back as proposed records next to the code (plumb capture), so clarifying and recording are one step. plumb clarify gives it the depth and drops drafted questions that records or defaults already answer.

examples.given: a request that maps to confirmed SR-004 with no flag
examples.then: depth is trivial and no question is returned

examples.given: the ambiguous request "let users export their data" and four drafted questions, one answered by a confirmed record and one whose options build the same thing
examples.then: exactly the two questions that matter are returned, ranked

examples.given: two decisions that matter recorded from questions asked outside a card
examples.then: only the first is asked in that message

examples.given: a request with two gaps, one with a better-supported answer
examples.then: the supported answer becomes a labelled assumption and only the other gap is raised, as one blocking choice card; the agent asks nothing more in that message

title: Untraced changes get a proposed owning requirement, never a written link
statement: For an untraced changed path, plumb proposes the owning requirement chosen by the judge model among candidates narrowed by the code map, in the agent's read-back instruction; with no judge to choose, it lists the candidates, says judging is unavailable naming the cause, and proposes none by rule (INT-029). At commit, a "does this diff serve its claimed SRs?" judgment may print a non-blocking warning and never changes the trailer check's result; with no judge it says judging is unavailable and warns nothing by rule. A verified_by link to a bare test file gets a proposed test node as a drift hint. None of these writes a link.

examples.given: src/app/mul.py changed with no owner, SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py in the same package, and the judge picks SR-001 among the candidates
examples.then: it names SR-001 as the proposed owner and no link is added

examples.given: a commit claiming SR-004 that only changes src/app/report.py
examples.when: the commit-msg hook runs with a backend answering no
examples.then: it prints a warning and exits 0

examples.given: SR-001 verified_by tests/test_calc.py with test_add_returns_sum inside
examples.then: a hint proposes tests/test_calc.py::test_add_returns_sum for EX-1

examples.given: SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py and src/app/mod.py is written and not committed and the judge picks SR-001
examples.then: its drift section names SR-001 as the proposed owner of src/app/mod.py, reading uncommitted changes as plumb merge-check does

examples.given: no judge model is configured, src/app/mul.py changed with no owner and SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py
examples.then: it lists SR-001 as a candidate, says judging is unavailable naming judgment.backend, proposes no owner and adds no link

examples.given: no judge model is configured
examples.when: the diff-serves check runs for a commit claiming SR-004 that only changes src/app/report.py
examples.then: it prints one line that judging is unavailable and no warning decided by rule

title: A bounded hidden-dependency scan shows records that may silently depend on a change, as hints only
statement: When a confirmed record or an authoritative document changes, a scan of at most 5 candidates and 1 second proposes records or documents with no link to it that may depend on what changed, confirmed by the backend, and returns them as drift hints; they are never staleness marks, edges or interruptions.

examples.given: confirmed SR-004 changes and SR-012 shares its key terms with no link

title: events.jsonl and evidence.jsonl are migrated without breaking the...
statement: plumb log migrate moves every line of events.jsonl and evidence.jsonl into per-entry files with the same fields, so every digest, prev link and evidence identity (run ids, node evidence, approval references) is unchanged; migrated files are named from the entry's time and digest, so the migration is idempotent and two branches that migrate independently merge cleanly; the legacy files are emptied, not deleted, so a branch made before the migration still merges; a line whose digest does not match is never migrated and the command refuses; until every line is migrated, readers accept both formats, deduplicated by digest.

examples.then: 510 entry files exist, each with the digest and prev of its line, and plumb validate is clean

examples.then: no file is written or changed

examples.given: a branch created before the migration that appended two lines to events.jsonl
examples.when: it is merged after the migration
examples.then: git merges without conflict, readers see both lines, and the next migration moves them into files

examples.then: plumb verify reuses the same evidence and the same tests stay fresh

examples.given: a legacy line edited by hand
examples.then: it refuses, names the line and writes nothing

title: Record files merge field by field
statement: plumb hooks install declares a merge driver for record files (in .plumb/.gitattributes and the repository's git config, idempotent, removed by uninstall); the driver merges a record field by field against the merge base, so non-overlapping changes merge automatically: links added on either side, independent fields, list items and examples added on both sides (a clashing new EX number is renumbered inside the record), and formatting differences never conflict.

examples.given: one side adds a verified_by link to SR-005 and the other side adds an implemented_by link
examples.then: SR-005 has both links and nothing conflicts

examples.given: one side changes SR-005's title and the other adds an example EX-4
examples.then: the result has the new title and EX-4, with no intent conflict

examples.given: both sides add a new example numbered EX-3 with different content
examples.then: the incoming one becomes EX-4 and its verified_by link's example is rewritten to EX-4

examples.given: plumb hooks install ran twice
examples.then: the plumb-record driver is declared once and other attributes are kept

title: A content conflict becomes an intent conflict the owner resolves
statement: When both sides change the same field of a record differently (a statement, a title, an example, the body), the driver keeps the record parseable and writes an intent conflict (IC-###) into it holding the base, both versions and both branch labels; the record's hash then matches neither side, so it stays unconfirmed; plumb shows it as one conflict card with both versions and what merged on its own, with an optional JEV compatibility judgment that is advisory; only the owner chooses (mine, theirs, or a combined wording), in the owner's terminal or by the owner's own words relayed and checked like an approval, and the choice is logged.

examples.given: main changed SR-005's statement one way and feat-x changed it another way
examples.then: SR-005 carries IC-001 with both statements and the labels main and feat-x, and SR-005 is unconfirmed

examples.given: IC-001 is open
examples.when: /plumb review or the merge check shows it
examples.then: one conflict card shows both statements, what merged on its own and the owner's choices in plain words

examples.given: the owner says "keep feat-x's version"
examples.then: SR-005 takes feat-x's statement, the conflict block is gone, a resolution event records the owner's quote, and SR-005 is confirmed again if feat-x's version was confirmed

examples.when: the agent runs the choice in its shell
examples.then: it is refused with exit 3 and nothing changes

examples.given: JEV is not configured
examples.then: it says no compatibility judgment is available, and choosing works the same

examples.given: SR-005 still carries the open conflict IC-001 (main's statement against feat-x's)
examples.when: feat-y, which changed SR-005 again where main also changed it, is merged
examples.then: git leaves SR-005 unmerged with both versions in the file: IC-001 and feat-x's statement are kept, and no new conflict replaces them

title: A quick merge check holds open intent conflicts
statement: plumb check --merge and plumb merge-check list every open intent conflict as a card and wait for the owner's choice (exit 4). /plumb init and plumb hooks install also install, by default, a quick merge-time check as git's pre-merge-commit and prepare-commit-msg hooks (R17): it holds a merge carrying an open intent conflict, a touched requirement not yet confirmed, a file no requirement declares or two records holding one ID, however the merge is recorded (git merge, git pull, or git commit finishing it), and a rebase, cherry-pick or revert step carrying an open intent conflict; it judges what git will record and runs no test suite (the one full run happens at push, in the pre-push hook); a foreign hook is left untouched.

title: Awareness reads other worktrees read-only, cheaply and cached
statement: Each worktree's hooks publish the records its branch is changing to its own gitignored .plumb/cache/changing.json, recomputed only when its HEAD or its changed paths moved; other worktrees read those files and git's worktree and ref files directly, never writing into another worktree, taking a lock or holding a lease; branches without a worktree are scanned at session start only, within a time cap, and cached by branch tip; the overlap check adds at most 50 ms to a warm hook.

examples.when: the prompt hook computes overlaps with warm caches
examples.then: it takes under 50 ms and starts no git process

examples.then: no git command runs for that branch

examples.then: no file in that worktree is created or modified

examples.then: that worktree is ignored

examples.then: feat-x is not named as changing SR-005

title: Intent in flight is shared through refs/plumb/claims
statement: When a worktree captures a change to an existing record or new intent in a feature, plumb records a lightweight claim in the shared ref refs/plumb/claims (git compare-and-swap, shared by every worktree of the repository): the records, their features, the branch and a one-line summary of the intent. A claim is a signal, never a lock: nothing is refused because of it. It clears when its branch is merged into the default branch or deleted, or when the owner drops that work (ruling R17).

examples.then: refs/plumb/claims holds a claim naming SR-005, branch feat-x and a one-line summary of the request

examples.then: both claims are kept and no update is lost

examples.when: feat-x is merged into main, or deleted
examples.then: the claim no longer appears in the register

examples.when: this worktree edits or captures SR-005
examples.then: nothing is refused, locked or held; plumb only informs

title: Intent conflicts are caught at capture, before any implementation
statement: plumb capture and plumb clarify check the other branches' claims before any implementation. The same record claimed elsewhere is caught deterministically; new intent in a feature another branch claims is judged for compatibility by the configured judge (JEV when configured). No rule-based judge stands in for one that cannot be reached (INT-029): the line or card then says why it could not judge ("judging unavailable: <cause>"), and the overlap is treated as unsure, never as compatible; a merge conflict card likewise shows the cause, never a rule-based verdict. A contradiction shows an early intent-conflict card ("feat-x says A, this request says B: which one, or both?") and is recorded once as a proposed decision that matters, so the owner is asked at once and every branch sees the question and its answer; a compatible overlap gives only a one-line warning (ruling R17). The owner's answers to these cards go through the reader (SP8), or an exact typed pick of a branch's name; no word rules read them.

examples.when: this worktree captures a different change to SR-005
examples.then: an early conflict card shows feat-x's version and this request's version, and one proposed decision that matters decides SR-005

title: plumb installs as a Claude Code plugin and runs its own private copy of its tools
statement: plumb's repository offers plumb as a Claude Code plugin: the /plumb command, the plumb and plumb-clarify skills, plumb's background checks (at session start, on each message, after each edit, at the end of each answer, and the guard that keeps the agent from confirming for you) and the in-app panels. Installed with Claude Code's own plugin commands, all of it is built into every project. Everything the plugin runs uses plumb's own private copy of its tools, kept per user and per plugin version and built from the copy of plumb the plugin carries; never the project's own development setup (ruling R15).

examples.given: a machine with Claude Code and uv but no plumb anywhere
examples.when: the owner adds plumb's plugin list and installs the plumb plugin with Claude Code's plugin commands, then opens a session in any project
examples.then: /plumb, the plumb skills and the background checks are available, and nothing was written into that project

examples.when: any background check, the /plumb command or an in-app panel runs plumb
examples.then: it runs the plugin's own copy of plumb and uses nothing from the project's setup

title: /plumb init adopts a project; projects not adopted stay silent

Nothing of Claude Code's (commands, skills, background checks) is copied into the project. In a project plumb has not adopted, the plugin stays silent apart from one line per session: "/plumb init to adopt this repository" (rulings R15, R17).

examples.then: plumb's record folder exists, git's checks at commit, merge and push each call plumb's launcher, git knows how to merge plumb's records, and the project's Claude Code settings are unchanged

The card setting full, compact or off applies, and all of its text speaks at the owner's level (ruling R19).

A typed "ok" still works. title: Every owner action has an owner entry point; plumb's internal...
statement: Every capability the owner acts on or needs to see is reachable through a typed /plumb command, a button, or the owner's message read by the reader, and the agent does the rest. plumb's internal mechanisms (linking, repinning, hashing, test selection, log upkeep, ID sync and the like) stay internal: plumb and the agent run them, the owner is never asked to, and owner-facing text never mentions them. Owner-only actions (confirming and undoing, a group, a big plan, picking one of two versions, automatic confirmation on or off, the settings view, skipping the full test run) come only from the owner: words or a /plumb command the owner typed, which plumb saw arrive, or a button press. An action the agent starts on its own is refused. When the agent carries out the owner's typed words or command, plumb records it as passed on by the agent with the owner's exact words, so the owner can tell it apart from a button press. A typed /plumb approve or confirm naming IDs stays an exact owner action and confirms those records at once, recorded as passed on from the owner's typed command; /plumb confirm takes IDs only. The owner's plain prose is never matched to records by plumb's own word rules: it goes through the reader (SR-101), which decides what each record shown to the owner got. One table lists every owner action with the owner's way to reach it, and an end-to-end test drives every owner flow only through /plumb commands, messages and button presses (ruling R14).

title: Owner-visible text names no shell command and speaks at the owner's level
statement: No text the owner sees (the README and owner guides, cards, summaries, the band and status line, background-check messages, /plumb answers, error messages, merge and push reports, git's check messages, the Obsidian vault, and the content of the records the owner confirms) names a shell command; it names the /plumb command or the plain words to say. All of it speaks at the owner's level: goals, behaviours and the owner's words, never plumb's or the code's inner workings (internal codes, record numbers without their titles, folder and file names, test names) unless the owner asks; an idea that is genuinely needed is explained first in one plain sentence. One place holds plumb's wording for the owner, two checks (shell commands, inner workings) test every surface, and records are checked when the agent writes them, so the agent rewords them before the owner ever sees them (rulings R14, R18).

title: An unrelated request in the same message never blocks an ok
statement: When plumb reads which records an owner's message confirms, objections and changes count only in the sentence that holds the ok and in sentences that name, or plainly refer to, the records being confirmed, whether the ok names them by number or is a bare ok after they were shown. An unrelated request in the same message neither blocks the confirmation nor counts as a reservation, and the words passed on need not include it. A correction in the ok's own sentence, a reservation about the shown records, and an objection that refers to them in general still hold the ok back. Every place plumb reads an ok (single records, a group, a big plan, picking a version, the suggestion to the agent and the merge glance) reads the same scope (ruling R16).

title: A bare "yes" or option letter remembers what it answered
statement: When the owner's words behind an intent or an example are only a yes or an option letter ("yes", "A", "ok"), the record remembers what was answered: the question or the proposal, exactly as it was shown. plumb refuses to record a bare answer that does not say what it answered, or that points to something never shown. Cards show: you said "A" to: the question or proposal in plain words. Automatic confirmation counts a bare yes only when the owner accepted a single proposal whole; picking among options never makes the question count as the owner's own words (ruling R18.1).

title: The clarify read-back questions itself and labels assumptions instead of asking
statement: plumb-clarify questions its own read-back before showing it: unexamined absolutes, unstated tradeoffs, unsupported claims and contradictions become labelled assumptions by default, and a question only when the answer changes what gets built. plumb gives these to the agent as hints. Nothing is recorded for them and nothing waits on them. The read-back speaks at the owner's level (ruling R18.2).

title: An intent can say when it is done
statement: An intent may say when it is done: a short list in the owner's terms. When the agent clarifies a request, plumb tells the agent (never the owner) what the request leaves open: its scope (what will be done), its non-goals (what won't), its success (when it is done) and its failure cases (examples of errors or refusals). plumb's alignment check names every "done when" item that no example covers yet (ruling R18.3).

examples.then: the intent card shows "Done when: you get a reminder three days before each deadline"

examples.then: it names that item as a gap in plain words

examples.given: an example that covers that "done when" item
examples.then: the gap is gone

title: A big plan is checked and repaired before the owner is offered it
statement: Before a big plan (an escalated set of records) is offered for confirmation, plumb checks its structure: every part comes from the plan's intent, every "will" is served by a requirement, every requirement has an example, every "done when" item has an example, and nothing goes against a "won't" (plumb's judge decides that one). The agent fixes every gap in the structure itself and checks again until the plan is clean; the owner is asked only about intent or tradeoffs (a "will" that cannot be served without breaking a "won't", two incompatible readings, a scope choice). The offer to confirm (the summary's offer line, /plumb confirm of the plan, a Confirm button) appears only for a clean plan, and an ok passed on for a plan that is not clean is refused (ruling R18.4).

examples.given: a big plan where one requirement has no example
examples.then: the gap goes to the agent, no offer is shown, the agent adds the example, and the next check is clean and shows the offer

examples.given: a plan whose "will" "email the reminders" goes against its "won't" "keep email addresses"
examples.then: the owner is asked one question about that tradeoff, recorded as a decision that matters

examples.then: it is refused, naming the gaps to the agent

examples.given: any gap the agent can fix
examples.then: the owner never sees it

title: A requirement left with two versions after a merge is shown once, as a choice
statement: When a merge leaves a requirement with two versions to choose from, plumb reports it once, on its choice card, and never as a list of its connected work that changed: the merge check, plumb's integrity check, the drift report, the status, the turn summary, the review and the Obsidian vault all show it under the choice. Once the owner's choice is recorded, plumb refreshes what it remembers about the requirement's connections, so nothing about it remains (leftover from sub-project 6).

examples.then: the merge waits, shows the choice between the two versions of "deadline reminders", and lists nothing else about it

title: A reader model works out the owner's answer to each record shown
statement: A model independent of the coding agent reads the owner's logged free-prose message against the records the previous reply showed (each at its version) and the open cards, in one read job per turn, and returns per item: accepted, rejected (misread or intent changed), change asked (what), or open, with the words that carry it and its own confidence from 0 to 1; a card's resolutions map onto these four answers. plumb confirms an item only when the message is in the prompt log, the item was shown at that version, the evidence occurs in the message, and the answer is accepted with a confidence at or above the reader's threshold, which is learned from the owner's trial answers (0.9 until enough are on file); the confirmation records the owner's words. While the read job runs the status line says "reading your answer" and the agent goes on with nothing confirmed. Only the hook-started worker applies a result, from job inputs it recomputed from the logs; a file the agent writes confirms nothing. A typed /plumb approve or confirm naming IDs is an exact owner action that bypasses the reader and confirms at once; an agent-run prose relay no longer exists. Fixed rules (affirmation words, objection words, clause splitting, plain-words matching) are not used to understand the owner, and owner-only settings and Undo change only by a typed command or a button.

examples.then: INT-008 is confirmed with the words "INT-008 ok" and SR-088 gets a change: some features stay internal to plumb

examples.then: nothing is confirmed and the item stays on its card

examples.then: nothing is confirmed and the new version is shown

examples.then: DEC-017 is confirmed at once, recorded as passed on from the owner's typed command, and the reader is not called

examples.then: the worker recomputes the job's inputs from the logs and applies only what it computed itself; the agent's file confirms nothing and is reported

examples.then: auto-approve stays off and nothing is undone; plumb replies with the typed command or button to use, because owner-only settings and Undo change only by a typed command or a button

examples.when: the agent runs plumb relay for SR-001 from its shell with a quote from that prompt
examples.then: plumb refuses and nothing is confirmed: an agent-run prose relay no longer exists; only the typed command and the worker confirm

title: A judge model decides whether a record is supported by the owner's...
statement: A model independent of the coding agent, asked whether the owner would object to the record given their words, judges each new or changed record (one judge job per capture covers all of them) against its premise (the owner's whole logged message or messages, the question a short answer answered, a parent intent the owner confirmed) and the owner's confirmed or settled records, leaving labelled assumptions out of what is judged, and returns supported, beyond (naming what the owner's words do not support) or contradicts (naming what and with which record), with its own confidence, logged with the verdict. The premise message is committed to the repository log (text and digest) when the record first takes it as premise, so it outlives the session. A supported verdict whose premise is an option picked among several is never settled; it goes to a trial or confirm card (SR-091).

examples.then: supported

title: The clarifier asks every blocking question up front, with the...
statement: On every owner message a model decides whether it starts or changes intent; if so it drafts the read-back with will, won't, assumptions and two or three concrete examples, and finds the gaps that change what gets built; if not it returns no intent and there is no card. Per SR-131 a gap with a better-supported answer becomes a labelled assumption, and the owner gets at most one blocking choice card per turn, with suggested answers and a recommended one; assumptions stay labelled and proposed, and a choice answer confirms nothing by itself (per SR-130 the read-back's ok confirms its records). More than one blocking question with no better-supported answer escalates to a short spec session; a request with no such gap produces no card and work starts at once. The agent's first action is plumb clarify --wait, which returns the result, waiting up to a timeout for the job; until the result for the latest owner message is collected the guard refuses edits, and the agent does not build until a card is answered. This up-front block overrides INT-004's no-blocking only for gaps that change what gets built.

examples.then: each question no better-supported answer settles is asked with the question tool, with suggested answers, and the other gaps are labelled assumptions

examples.then: no question; work starts

examples.then: three questions are asked with the question tool, all before building; no spec session is offered for the count alone

examples.when: the reader maps it to rejected
examples.then: the guard stays closed and the next message retries the check

examples.then: the edit is refused, because the failed model is the one that would say whether the message carried intent, until the owner releases it or the next turn's retry succeeds

title: Model jobs run in the background through the host's own dispatch,...
statement: Reading and judging are jobs queued by the hooks and run by a background worker, so no hook waits on a model; jobs are batched (one read job per turn covering everything shown, one judge job per capture covering every record it wrote or changed) because each model start costs seconds; while a job runs the status line and, in a terminal or shell, a bar or plain lines say its current step in plain words and its progress (SR-108); the clarify job is queued by the hook too and is collected by the agent's plumb clarify --wait outside any hook. Each job runs through the one configured dispatcher: Claude Code runs claude -p with a plumb agent selected by --agent, no tools, a small model, the job's answer schema and no user or project settings, MCP servers, skills or CLAUDE.md, in a neutral working directory, and plumb's hooks do nothing inside it; Hermes runs a delegated child session; OpenRouter only when configured. Only the hook-started worker applies results, and it recomputes every job's inputs from the logs, so a job file carries no authority. A dispatcher that fails makes the job fail with an error the owner sees; nothing is confirmed, settled or rejected and the job is retried on the next turn. There is never a second route or a rule-based fallback.

examples.given: the owner's message arrives
examples.then: it queues the read job and returns within its budget without waiting for the model

examples.given: the Claude Code dispatcher runs a job
examples.when: plumb's hooks fire inside that headless session
examples.then: they exit at once and queue nothing

examples.given: the configured model is unreachable
examples.then: the summary says plumb could not check the owner's answers, nothing is confirmed, and the job is retried next turn

examples.given: the same job inputs queued twice
examples.then: the job runs once

examples.given: the configured model is unreachable
examples.when: the worker runs the read job
examples.then: the word rules of approvals.py are not called and nothing is confirmed

examples.then: the command selects the plumb agent with --agent and passes --setting-sources empty, --strict-mcp-config and --disable-slash-commands, runs in an empty temporary directory, and the job's context holds no CLAUDE.md text

examples.then: the worker uses the inputs it recomputed from the logs, not the file's, so the file cannot make a record look supported

examples.given: a turn whose previous reply showed five records and one open card
examples.then: one read job covers all six items, not six jobs

examples.given: a capture that writes one intent and six requirements
examples.then: one judge job is queued for the seven records

examples.given: a read job takes eight seconds
examples.when: the owner looks at the status line
examples.then: it says "reading your answer" and the agent has carried on with nothing confirmed

examples.when: the owner looks at the status line
examples.then: it says "judging 7 records" with the progress, and the line disappears when the job ends

title: What awaits the owner comes as cards with suggested resolutions;...
statement: The end-of-turn summary shows the owner, in order: what they confirmed by their words, one line naming what was settled from their words (each with Undo), and cards; each card names the topic in the owner's terms, the issue, the evidence, and two or three suggested resolutions with the recommended one first, written by the agent from plumb's facts; card kinds are clarify, trial batch, backlog feature, goes beyond your words, contradicts, and couldn't check. A settled record counts as confirmed in status, the merge boundary and validation, and is listed apart. Undo is a button or the typed /plumb undo, never a model's reading of prose.

title: Settling starts with a trial that calibrates on the owner's answers
statement: Until calibration passes for a record kind, every supported record is offered in trial batches of up to five (plumb would settle these; right?); the owner's yes settles it and labels it yes, no rejects it as a misreading; calibration reruns from logged judgments after each batch; when it passes for requirements (with their examples), the records the agent derives, settling for that kind switches itself on, the owner is told once how to switch it off, and the switch-on is logged with the calibration that allowed it; when it passes for intents, the owner is told once and turns settling on with the typed /plumb settle on command or a button (prose cannot); the owner switches any kind off by the typed /plumb settle off or a button, and plumb never switches a kind on again that the owner switched off; settled records are labelled settled from your words, count as confirmed at the merge, are listed apart there, and return to proposed when their text or premise changes; a model or prompt change suspends settling until the evaluation set passes and calibration reruns, after which a kind that switched itself on does so again unless the owner switched it off. A decision never settles and is always asked individually, nor a set member, an escalated set member or an edit of an owner-confirmed record. JEV's own probability is logged as its score at judgment time, marked as JEV's (by: jev), and calibration reads only those, never the judge model's confidence (SR-182), so thresholds come from trial outcomes and are not fixed; the owner's trial yes and no, misread rejections and owner-words confirmations are the labels; one item per batch is drawn from below the threshold.

title: Drift is caught at the edit that causes it and resolved before the...

Before the turn can end, the agent resolves each one: it reruns the linked tests and repins when a model judges the meaning unchanged (INT-029), or rewords the dependent record so it agrees, or, when what the owner intended is in question, brings it to the owner as a card. The end-of-turn hook keeps the turn open while a link this turn made stale is unresolved, and says which. Links stale before the turn are listed to the agent once, not blocking.

title: Only the owner confirms a record: their typed command, a button,...
statement: A record is confirmed only by the owner: a typed /plumb approve or confirm naming IDs, a button press, an owner-only command in their own terminal after a y/N answered there, or the owner's free-prose message read by the reader (SR-101), which confirms an item only when the message is in the prompt log, the item was shown in full at that version and the reader accepted it with enough confidence. No fixed words (affirmation, objection, scope or reservation rules) are used to understand the owner, and an agent-run relay of the owner's prose no longer exists. The session marker refuses plumb approve and plumb revoke for the agent, and on every host an owner-only command writes only after a y/N answered in an interactive terminal, so an agent shell without the marker is refused too; silence confirms nothing, and an unclear reading confirms nothing and asks once.

title: A code change that no longer matches an aligned record goes to the...
statement: When a stale link's change alters what a requirement relies on, plumb first checks whether the requirement still agrees with the intent it derives from. If the requirement and its intent disagree, the record is reworded or brought to the owner as before. If they agree, the code moved away from the owner's intent: the owner gets a card by title, in the owner's words, with two lines of context (SR-129), naming the intent, the requirement and the change, unless the change plainly should not have been made (it breaks an example with no request behind it), in which case it goes back to the agent with the change, its turn and the requirement it breaks, to be fixed as development work rather than asked about.

title: The repin check is a cascade: JEV clears the easy links, Sonnet...

Otherwise Sonnet judges with the requirement and the diff, and its unchanged verdict repins. When Sonnet says the change matters, Opus investigates instead of judging again: it checks the requirement against its intent and the change against the turn that made it (SR-113), and prepares either a rewording of the record, the change sent back to development, or a card asking the owner to decide, saying what is wrong in plain words.

examples.then: its proof is a live session capture showing the drawing

examples.given: a requirement whose proof has run
examples.when: the owner runs plumb show on it
examples.then: the proof and its evidence (where to see it) are printed

examples.given: a branch with one requirement whose proof was never shown
examples.then: it names that requirement as not shown working, and the merge is not blocked by it

title: The request check reads the request with its conversation
statement: When the owner types /plumb clarify, the check receives the agent's last reply, the owner's recent messages and the repository facts, and uses them to resolve references to earlier turns

examples.given: the agent's last reply listed review findings
examples.when: the owner says 'resolve all of the findings using a workflow'
examples.then: no card asks which findings

examples.given: the agent diagnosed why the panel does not show
examples.when: the owner says 'apply the proposed fixes for this issue'
examples.then: no card asks which issue

examples.given: the repository is a git repository
examples.then: it never says the folder is not a git repository

examples.given: the transcript cannot be read
examples.then: it runs on the message alone as before

examples.given: the owner refers to an issue found in another recent chat of the same project ('the issue we detected in that chat')
examples.then: it reads that chat's last reply and the owner's last messages there, and no card asks which issue

examples.given: the conversation was compacted
examples.then: the agent's last reply and the compaction summary are given, and the summary is never taken as the owner's words

title: A card is a read-back or a choice, and stands alone
statement: Every card the owner sees is either the read-back of one request (proposal in the owner's words, flippable assumptions, at most one won't) or one choice (one question, options each with a one-line consequence, the recommended option first, two lines saying which request raised it and what changes with the answer); it is readable with no memory of the conversation, in the owner's words, with no ids, digests or plumb vocabulary

examples.given: a request whose read-back has five will lines, two won't, four assumptions and three examples
examples.then: the card has the proposal in one to three sentences, the assumptions the owner could disagree with, and the one won't that rules out something expected; examples, ids and the quote are left to plumb show

examples.given: a card read the next day from the backlog
examples.then: it names the request it came from with its date and what changes with the answer, and needs nothing from the conversation

examples.given: a card's text contains 'settled', 'trial', a record id or a digest
examples.then: that word is not on the card: the owner's own terms are used instead

examples.given: an agent files a stale-link card lacking options, consequences or the reason for the recommended one (SR-116 EX-3)
examples.then: the card is refused as incomplete and the agent is told what is missing

title: A record is confirmed through its read-back, never asked about alone
statement: The records a read-back creates are confirmed by the owner's answer to that read-back; a record is re-asked only when it changed or a merge brought a second version, and then as a choice showing both versions side by side

examples.given: a read-back that created an intent, two requirements and a decision
examples.then: all four are confirmed by that one answer and no card asks about any of them again

examples.given: a decision changed since the owner saw it
examples.when: the owner presses No on the old card
examples.then: the owner sees one choice card with the version they answered and the new one side by side, never a title with yes/no

examples.given: a merge brings two versions of one requirement
examples.then: one choice card shows both versions and what each means, with 'keep this one', 'keep the other' and 'both' as options

title: A recommendable option is an assumption; every gap without one is...
statement: When the commanded check (/plumb clarify) can recommend an option, it writes the recommendation as a flippable assumption on the read-back and the agent builds on; a gap is asked only when no option is better supported by the conversation, the records and the code and a wrong pick is costly to undo; every such gap is asked in the same turn with Claude Code's question tool, specific, with its options, and a vague answer is asked again

examples.given: the owner says 'resolve all the findings using a workflow' right after the agent listed review findings
examples.then: no question: the read-back assumes 'the findings I listed above' and the work starts

examples.given: a request that could change a public interface two ways, neither favoured by any record or the conversation
examples.then: one question is asked with the question tool, with both ways and what each costs to undo

examples.given: a request with three open gaps, each with a recommended option
examples.then: three assumption lines on the read-back and no question

examples.given: the owner answers a question with 'whatever works'
examples.then: the question is asked again and a pick is still needed; no option is taken for the owner

examples.given: a request with two gaps and no better-supported option for either
examples.when: the check returns them to the agent
examples.then: both are asked with the question tool in the same turn, not one per turn and not on a card

title: A card lives as long as its request
statement: An unanswered card is withdrawn when a newer read-back on the same thing replaces it or when its branch is merged; the merge summary names in one line the records that went in unconfirmed; a withdrawn card confirms nothing and its records stay proposed

examples.given: a card asking which findings to resolve, then a newer request naming them
examples.then: the older card is withdrawn and only the new one, if any, is open

examples.given: a branch with two open cards
examples.then: both are withdrawn and the merge summary says 'went in unconfirmed: <titles>' once

examples.given: a card from a previous session whose branch is gone
examples.then: it is not in the backlog

examples.given: a withdrawn card
examples.then: its records are still listed as proposed

title: A trial card is the read-back of one record
statement: A trial card shows the owner's source words found by meaning with their date, or says they were not found; the record's proposal in the owner's terms, including a decision's chosen option and its alternative; and Yes, No, Fix it; at most three trial cards are open at a time. Each press is a labelled owner answer, so Yes confirms the record (by owner, via button, label yes); No marks plumb's reading wrong, counts as a real 'no' for calibration, and the record stays; each button names its own record's offer, so a press from an out-of-date draw cannot land on another record; a card left open is not asked again until its record changes

examples.given: a decision whose source words are in a transcript of 4 Oct
examples.then: the card quotes those words with the date, states the chosen option and the alternative, and offers Yes, No, Fix it

examples.given: a record whose source words were not found
examples.then: it says the words were not found and shows the proposal alone, never an unrelated message

examples.given: five records eligible for a trial
examples.then: three are open, and the next one opens when one is answered

examples.given: three open trial cards
examples.when: the owner presses Yes on the first, No on the second and Yes on the third
examples.then: two approvals by owner via button labelled yes and one capture-error rejection are logged, the records stay, and after the next turn end jev status counts 1 real 'no' and 2 yes

examples.given: a trial card the owner pressed Leave open on
examples.then: the card is open again and repeats in the next draw; while nothing changed it stays left open

title: Records are confirmed by one judge path or by the owner, never by...
statement: A proposed record becomes confirmed only by the owner's words or button, or by the judge that reads the owner's words when auto-approve is on and calibrated; no record is settled from tests, links and a model's consistency check alone

examples.given: a requirement whose linked code exists, whose tests pass and that a model finds consistent
examples.when: the end of a turn runs
examples.then: it stays proposed and no 'settled by context' line or offer card appears

examples.given: the owner types /plumb settle on intent
examples.then: plumb says that switch no longer exists and nothing changes

examples.given: auto-approve is on and calibrated, and the owner says 'ok' to a read-back
examples.then: the read-back's records are confirmed, logged with the judge's verdict

title: Dead and doubled confirmation paths are gone
statement: plumb has no relay command, no triage offer at session start, no plumb confirm intent card, no prose copy of a card's question, no regex decoding of button labels, and no replay-proof for typed commands: typed settle, undo and go are handled at the prompt hook like approve

examples.given: the agent runs plumb relay
examples.then: it is refused as no longer existing, with no help line

examples.given: a button whose label was reworded
examples.then: its stored answer applies; nothing is decoded from the label

examples.given: the owner types /plumb undo SR-034
examples.then: the undo is done by the hook; the agent runs nothing and no --prompt digest exists for it

examples.given: a session start with low-risk records
examples.then: no triage offer asks the owner to say ok

title: The pane draws a diagram the skill produced, on every surface
statement: Given an HTML file or a bare SVG written with the architecture-diagram skill, the diagram pane draws it as Svg on the desktop app and VS Code, and in the terminal as box-drawing text with the same boxes, labels and arrows, readable at 110 columns; a file that holds no SVG is refused with a plain line saying so

examples.given: the skill's example diagram with eight component boxes and nine arrows
examples.then: the pane shows eight boxes with their labels and nine arrows between the right boxes, nothing overlapping

examples.given: the same file
examples.when: the pane is drawn on the desktop app
examples.then: it is the file's SVG, drawn as one Svg element

examples.given: a box whose label is wider than the box at terminal scale
examples.when: it is drawn in the terminal
examples.then: the label wraps or is cut with an ellipsis inside the box; no character overlaps another

examples.given: a file with no <svg>
examples.then: the pane says the file holds no diagram and draws nothing else

title: The skill is shipped and produces diagrams from a codebase
statement: The plugin ships the architecture-diagram skill with its licence; /diagram of <words> has the agent read the relevant code and write the diagram with that skill, saved under .diagram/ in the working folder, then shown in the pane

examples.given: /diagram of plumb's hooks
examples.then: an HTML file with inline SVG exists under .diagram/ and the pane shows it

examples.given: the shipped skill folder
examples.then: it holds SKILL.md, the template and the MIT licence, nothing else

title: The mod is shown working before it is called done
statement: A live Claude Code session on this terminal with the plugin loaded shows a diagram in the pane and the capture is kept as proof; the plugin passes claude plugin validate and its tests on the terminal and desktop surfaces

examples.given: claude --plugin-dir <the plugin> in a scratch folder
examples.then: the captured screen shows the pane with boxes and arrows

examples.given: the plugin folder
examples.then: it passes

title: A card can show a block diagram beside its question
statement: A card whose record names a diagram file shows that diagram above its question: the file's SVG as one picture on the desktop app and VS Code, box-drawing text in the terminal, through the diagram mod's drawing code; when the diagram mod is not installed, the card shows the question alone and one line naming the file

examples.given: a choice card about which hook writes host.json, with a six-box diagram of the hooks written with the skill
examples.when: the card is shown in the terminal
examples.then: the six boxes and their arrows sit above the question and the options, nothing overlapping, and the answer buttons still work

examples.given: the same card on the desktop app
examples.then: the diagram is the file's SVG as one picture above the question

examples.given: the same card in a session without the diagram mod
examples.then: the question and options show, with one line naming the diagram file to open

examples.given: a read-back card with no diagram
examples.then: nothing changes from today

title: The agent draws a diagram when the question is about structure or flow
statement: When the clarify step raises a question about which parts talk to which, an order of steps or where something lives, it tells the agent to draw the answer space with the architecture-diagram skill under .plumb/session/<id>/diagrams/ and to name the file on the card; a question about wording or scope gets no diagram

examples.given: a question asking which of three hooks should write host.json
examples.then: the agent writes a diagram of the three hooks and the file, and the card names it

examples.given: a question asking whether 'the findings' means the ones listed above
examples.then: no diagram is asked for

title: The clarify card prints its questions, not the read-back's lines
statement: When the hook prints a clarify card, before building or at the end of a turn, the card holds the topic, the questions and the suggested answers; the read-back's will, won't, assumed and example lines are not printed, though they stay on the stored card so answering it still confirms the assumptions

examples.given: a clarify card with two questions and a read-back of four will lines, one won't and two assumptions
examples.then: the output has the topic line, the two questions and the suggested answers, and no line starting with 'I will', 'I will not', 'Assumed' or 'For example'

examples.given: the same card
examples.then: the two labelled assumptions are confirmed exactly as before

examples.given: a stale-link card whose evidence says a test passed earlier and fails now
examples.then: its evidence line is printed as before

title: plumb unlink removes one link and says why
statement: plumb unlink <record#n> --note <why> removes link n from the record, renumbers the links after it, logs an unlink event with the removed link, its pin, the note and the renumbering, and prints each new link id

examples.given: SR-124 has links #0..#22 and #5 points at plugin/hooks/trial.test.tsx, which no longer exists
examples.when: plumb unlink SR-124#5 --note "the test moved to tests/plugin/mod" runs
examples.then: SR-124 has 22 links, the old #6 is now #5, the output lists each renumbered link, and the events log holds one unlink entry naming SR-124#5, its target, pin and note

examples.given: a record with no link #40
examples.then: it exits 1 saying there is no link SR-124#40, and the record file is unchanged

examples.given: any link
examples.then: it exits with a usage error and changes nothing
