examples.given: a link that is the only verified_by link of an example the owner confirmed, and its target still exists
examples.then: it is refused, saying the confirmed example would lose its only test and naming plumb relink instead; the record is unchanged

examples.given: a dangling link that is the only verified_by link of a confirmed example
examples.then: it is removed (a dangling link proves nothing) and the output says the example now has no test

title: plumb relink moves one link to a new target
statement: plumb relink <record#n> <target> --note <why> keeps the link's number, kind and example, points it at the new target with fresh pins on both ends, and logs a relink event with the old and new targets and pins

examples.given: SR-124#5 verified_by plugin/hooks/trial.test.tsx (dangling) for no example
examples.then: SR-124#5 is verified_by tests/plugin/mod/trial.test.tsx, pinned to the file and record as they are now, and the events log holds one relink entry with both targets

examples.given: a new target that does not exist
examples.then: it exits 1 naming the missing target and the record is unchanged

examples.given: the record already has the same kind, target and example as another link
examples.when: plumb relink would make link n a copy of it
examples.then: it is refused, naming the existing link and suggesting plumb unlink

examples.given: a kind that cannot point at the new target (a record-only kind given a file)
examples.then: it is refused with the same message plumb link gives

title: A conflict is answered on its card, never relayed by the agent
statement: plumb conflict relay and conflict choose with --prompt/--quote are refused as no longer existing; the phrase matching that read the owner's words for them is gone; the owner answers a conflict on its card or with their own typed choose

examples.given: an open merge conflict
examples.when: the agent runs plumb conflict relay with the owner's quoted words
examples.then: it is refused as no longer existing, exit 3, and nothing is chosen

examples.given: the same conflict
examples.when: the owner presses 'Keep main's version' on its card
examples.then: main's version is chosen exactly as before

examples.given: the skills and the command's allowed tools
examples.then: no conflict relay or quoted choose is named

title: Conflict cards are drawn by the one card renderer
statement: Merge and early conflict cards reach the owner through the same renderer as every other card: the record by its title, each side in words, the options each with what it does, no conflict or record ids; the agent's plumb conflicts view keeps the ids it needs

examples.given: a merge conflict on a requirement between main and a branch
examples.when: its card is drawn at the end of a turn and in the panel
examples.then: it names the requirement by title, shows both versions and a proposed combined one with what each choice does, and no IC- or SR- id appears

examples.given: the same conflict
examples.then: it still lists the conflict id it needs for plumb conflict propose

examples.given: an early conflict between two worktrees
examples.then: it has the same shape and no ids

title: The judge's doubts are lines on the read-back, not cards
statement: When the judge finds a record goes beyond or contradicts the owner's words, the request's read-back card gets one line saying so in the second person, and no separate card is raised for that record

examples.given: a request whose read-back recorded a requirement the owner never asked for
examples.when: the judge reads it as going beyond their words
examples.then: the read-back card has a line 'You did not ask for <title>; Yes confirms it too, so choose Not quite to drop it' and no card is raised for that record

examples.given: a record that contradicts a confirmed one
examples.then: the read-back line names both by title and says which one you confirmed

examples.given: a request with no such finding
examples.then: it is unchanged

examples.given: a doubt about a record of one request, and the read-back of another request
examples.then: it does not carry the line; the line goes only on its own request's read-back

title: Repeated worker bookkeeping avoids redundant file access
statement: Plumb reduces repeated log-head reads and replacements, log lock churn, and unchanged progress writes while preserving durable hash-chained entries, worker authority, fresh events between jobs, and timely progress and completion reporting.

examples.given: a valid log head and a job with multiple verdicts
examples.then: every verdict remains a separate valid chained entry and bounded batches reduce head and lock operations

examples.given: a batch interrupted after some entries have been persisted
examples.then: it recovers the persisted head and extends the actual chain without trusting an older pointer

examples.given: repeated identical running progress updates
examples.when: updates occur within the heartbeat interval
examples.then: redundant writes are coalesced while changed counts and final or failed states are written immediately

examples.given: multiple backlog jobs in one worker pass
examples.then: later jobs observe those events and final progress and cards reflect the complete pass

title: Only requests about the system being built raise a card
statement: The commanded request check (/plumb clarify) raises a read-back or question card only for a message that starts or changes something in the repository's own system (behaviour, code, tests, docs, records); a message that operates Claude Code, tools or the machine, or only asks a question, raises no card and opens the hold

examples.given: the owner types '/plumb clarify claude plugin marketplace update plumb' and '/plumb clarify claude plugin update plumb@plumb'
examples.then: no card is raised and the hold opens

examples.given: the owner types '/plumb clarify are there anything to merge on main?'
examples.then: no card is raised

examples.given: the owner types '/plumb clarify make the status line show the branch name'
examples.then: a read-back card is raised as before

title: The card pane steps through what is waiting
statement: The pane, opened by the owner's click, shows one waiting card at a time with its diagram, and Back and Next buttons (with hotkeys) move between them, showing 'n of m'; when it is seated inline because the terminal cannot dock it, it says in one line how to get it beside the conversation

examples.given: three cards wait, the second carrying a diagram
examples.when: the owner opens the pane and presses Next
examples.then: the pane shows the second card with its diagram above its question and '2 of 3'

examples.given: the pane shows the last card
examples.then: it stays on the last card; Back moves to the one before

examples.given: no card waits
examples.then: it says nothing waits and draws no Back or Next

examples.given: a 100-column terminal
examples.then: it opens above the prompt with one line saying it docks on the right from 110 columns in the fullscreen layout

examples.given: the band only
examples.when: a turn ends with cards waiting
examples.then: no pane opens by itself

title: Answers to the question tool are kept as the owner's words
statement: When Claude Code's question tool returns the owner's answers, plumb logs each question, the options shown and the answer as the owner's words for the session; such an answer never confirms, rejects or changes a record

examples.given: the agent asks 'Run the slow tests now or later?' with the question tool
examples.then: plumb's log holds that question, both options and 'later' as the owner's answer in this session

examples.given: the owner's question-tool answer says 'yes, confirm SR-005'
examples.then: SR-005 is not confirmed: only a card press or the owner's typed command confirms

examples.given: the owner dismisses the question without answering
examples.then: nothing is logged as an answer

title: The question tool by default; a card only for a complex decision,...
statement: plumb's skills tell the agent to ask with Claude Code's question tool by default, and to use a card only for a complex decision: one whose answer must change the owner's records (confirm, conflict, stale link, a decision that matters) or that has more than one option with a real trade-off or a costly wrong pick; the card shows the full context and the pros and cons of each option, so the owner can study it

examples.given: the agent needs to know which of two files the owner meant
examples.then: it asks with the question tool

examples.given: a merge conflict on a record
examples.then: it leaves the conflict on its card and does not ask with the question tool

examples.given: a request that could change a public interface two ways, each with a cost to undo
examples.then: a card, with both ways, what each costs and what it keeps, so the owner can study it

examples.given: the agent needs to know now or later, a name, or which of two files
examples.then: the question tool asks it; no card

title: The agent can suggest how to resolve a conflict
statement: The agent can store a suggested resolution for a conflict (keep one side, or a combined version it proposes) with a one-line reason; the conflict card shows that option first, marked recommended, with the reason; the suggestion chooses nothing

examples.given: a merge conflict between main and feat-x on a requirement, where feat-x only fixes a typo main also has
examples.when: the agent suggests keeping feat-x's version because it only corrects the wording
examples.then: the card lists 'Keep feat-x's version' first, marked recommended, with that reason, and the conflict stays open until the owner presses

examples.given: the agent proposes a combined version and suggests it
examples.then: the combined version is first and recommended, with the agent's reason

examples.given: a conflict with no suggestion
examples.then: it shows no recommended option, as today

title: The end of a turn says in one plumb line what changed
statement: When the panel is running, the end-of-turn text carries no card content, only one short line from plumb, in plumb's colour where the host allows colour, saying what changed: new cards waiting, answers applied; with no panel, the cards are printed in full as before

examples.given: a turn that raised one new card, with the panel running
examples.then: the text shows one plumb line 'plumb: 1 new card waits on the panel' and no question or options

examples.given: the owner's answer on a card was applied during the turn
examples.then: one plumb line says the answer on that card was applied, by the card's title

examples.given: a session where the panel cannot run
examples.when: a turn ends with a card waiting
examples.then: the card is printed in full as before

examples.given: a turn where nothing about cards changed
examples.then: plumb prints nothing about cards

title: An answered card stops waiting at once, and cards are grouped by state
statement: Once the owner answers a card it no longer counts or shows as waiting, even before the answer is applied; the panel groups this session's cards as waiting for you, being processed, blocked (with the reason) and done

examples.given: the owner presses Yes on a card
examples.when: the next prompt or turn end lists cards waiting
examples.then: that card is not among them, and the panel shows it under 'done' once its answer is applied (under 'being processed' only while applying takes a noticeable time)

examples.given: an answer plumb cannot apply because the record changed since it was drawn
examples.then: the card shows under 'blocked' with that reason

examples.given: three cards waiting and none answered
examples.then: all three show under 'waiting for you' and the other groups are empty or hidden

title: A card whose question no longer stands is withdrawn by itself
statement: At each turn end, and right after plumb repin, relink or unlink, plumb withdraws a stale-link card whose link is current or no longer exists, and a read-back or trial card whose records are all confirmed or superseded; each withdrawal is logged and named in one line of the end-of-turn text

examples.given: a stale-link card for SR-111#18
examples.then: the card is withdrawn at once and the next turn end says 'Withdrawn: SR-111#18, its link is current again'

examples.given: a trial card for SR-150
examples.then: at the turn end the trial card is withdrawn with the reason that SR-150 is superseded

examples.given: a read-back card for INT-047 and its SR-155..157
examples.when: the owner confirms INT-047 and all three requirements
examples.then: the read-back card is withdrawn at the turn end

examples.given: a stale-link card whose link is still stale
examples.then: the card stays

title: plumb resolves from the confirmed records what they already...
statement: A background job, using the session's judge on its cheap model, reads each open card against the owner's confirmed records and withdraws a card only when a confirmed record answers it (quoting that record) or when it duplicates another open card; unsure keeps the card; it never answers a card and never counts a proposed record. The same reading runs before an issue becomes a card: a merge conflict, a stale link, an untraced change or a gap that a confirmed record or decision settles is resolved from it, logged with that record and undoable; only what the confirmed records do not settle is presented

examples.given: an open card asking whether a conflict may be answered through the agent in chat, and a confirmed decision saying it may
examples.then: the card is withdrawn, citing that decision's words

examples.given: the same card and only a proposed decision
examples.then: the card stays

examples.given: two open stale-link cards on SR-062 asking the same question
examples.then: one is withdrawn as a duplicate naming the other

examples.given: the judge cannot be reached
examples.then: nothing is withdrawn and one line says the check could not run

examples.given: a merge conflict on a requirement where a confirmed decision already chose one side's principle
examples.then: the side the decision implies is applied and logged with the decision; no card

examples.given: a stale link whose target moved but still covers the requirement, per its tests and a confirmed example
examples.then: the link is repinned silently and logged

examples.given: an issue the confirmed records do not settle, or two confirmed records that contradict
examples.then: it is presented to the owner, with the records it looked at

examples.given: no judge can be reached
examples.then: plumb says so and the issue is presented, not resolved by rule

title: A clear answer to a question is recorded once, never re-asked
statement: When the owner's message clearly answers a question just put to them (a card shown in text or in the panel, a question in the agent's last reply, or the question tool's last question), the request check records that answer with the question, closes the card it answers, and raises no new card for the message; an unclear or partial answer leaves the question open

examples.given: the agent showed the 'where you answer a conflict' card in text with options 1, 2 and 3
examples.then: the card is answered with option 2, citing '2', and no 'Your request: 2' card appears

examples.given: the agent's reply asked 'Merge now or after the review?'
examples.then: the answer is recorded with that question and no read-back card is raised for the reply

examples.given: a card with options 1, 2 and 3 shown in text
examples.when: the owner replies 'maybe 2, but I am not sure about the skills'
examples.then: the card stays open and nothing is recorded as its answer

examples.given: a card shown in text about SR-076 only
examples.then: only what that card showed is answered; no other record is confirmed

title: Requirements a redesign replaced are retired, and their links stop...
statement: A requirement another one supersedes is retired: its history stays, it no longer reaches the owner, and its links are not checked or reported as stale

examples.given: an old requirement (as SR-105 was) describes behaviour a newer one (SR-129) replaced
examples.when: the newer one is linked as superseding it
examples.then: the old one's links no longer appear among the stale links and no card is raised about them

examples.given: a requirement that still describes current behaviour but whose links moved
examples.then: it is repinned, not retired

title: A new intent names the existing requirements it changes, at capture
statement: When an intent is captured, plumb finds the existing requirements whose meaning the new intent changes or contradicts and names them, so they are superseded or reworded in the same capture instead of going stale later

examples.given: the card redesign's intent removes per-feature proposal cards and context settling
examples.then: plumb names the existing requirements that still describe those, such as the ones about proposal cards and settling, and the capture supersedes or rewords them

examples.given: a new requirement that says the agent relays the owner's conflict choice while another says it never does
examples.then: the contradiction is named before the work goes on

title: Problems with links are caught during the work and held at merge
statement: A change that leaves a link stale, links a file no test covers, or pins a version git never recorded is caught in the turn that makes it, also for agents a workflow runs, and a merge carrying new problems of these kinds is held

examples.given: a workflow agent changes code a requirement links to
examples.then: the stale link is reported to it to resolve, as it is to the main session

examples.given: a link pinned to a file version that was never committed
examples.then: the pinned version stays readable, so the link shows stale after the commit, is held like any other new stale link, and a repin can judge the change from the pinned text

examples.given: a merge that adds stale links or links to files no test covers
examples.then: the merge is held naming them

title: A record-changing question always has a card before the owner answers
statement: When the agent’s reply asks the owner something whose answer would confirm, reject or change a record, choose a conflict’s side or settle a stale link, plumb raises that question as a card at the turn end (from the reply, with its options) so the owner’s answer is read against it; when the owner answers such a question that has no card yet, plumb raises the card then and applies the answer to it, citing the owner’s words

examples.given: the agent’s reply asks: Reword SR-096 to follow INT-028, or keep it? with no card
examples.then: a choice card for SR-096 with those two options is in the owner’s panel, and the agent is told it was raised

examples.given: that card exists
examples.then: the card is answered with that option, citing the reply, and the agent is told; no new read-back card appears

examples.given: the agent asked such a question and the owner answered before any turn end raised a card
examples.when: the prompt hook reads the answer
examples.then: plumb raises the card from the question and applies the answer to it, in one step, logged with both

examples.given: the agent’s reply asks: Run the slow tests now or later?
examples.then: no card: the answer changes no record

title: Only the owner’s own typed words count as the owner’s
statement: The prompt log records each entry’s origin as the host marks it; a message from another session, a task notification or hook text is logged with that origin and is never read as the owner’s words: it closes or opens no gate, backs no capture quote, no approval and no card answer

examples.given: another Claude session sends this session a message
examples.then: the entry says it came from that session, the gate does not change, and plumb capture --prompt with its digest is refused as not the owner’s words

examples.given: a task notification arrives in the session
examples.then: it is not logged as the owner’s message and raises no request check

examples.given: the owner types a message
examples.then: it is logged as the owner’s, as today

title: The edit gate answers to this session’s own message, under one digest
statement: The gate that holds the agent’s edits is keyed by session and by the digest the prompt hook logged for the owner’s message; the request check and the gate use that same digest, so a check that answers ready opens the gate it closed, and a message in another session, even with the same text, never holds this one

examples.given: the owner types the same text in two sessions and one session’s card holds its gate
examples.when: the other session’s check answers ready
examples.then: the other session’s gate opens

examples.given: the hook logged the owner’s message under digest A
examples.then: it reports digest A and opens the gate closed under A; never a second digest for the same message

examples.given: the gate is closed by a question card
examples.then: the gate opens; no clarify rerun is needed

title: A conflict answered in chat is read by plumb, never relayed
statement: An owner’s chat reply to an open conflict card is read by plumb’s prompt hook against that card and applied when it clearly picks one version; plumb conflict relay and conflict choose --prompt/--quote are refused again as the agent’s

examples.given: a merge conflict card for SR-005 is open and the owner replies: keep feat-x’s version
examples.then: SR-005 takes feat-x’s version, the card closes citing the owner’s words, and nothing was run by the agent

examples.given: the same card
examples.when: the agent runs plumb conflict relay with the owner’s quote
examples.then: it is refused with exit 3 and nothing changes

examples.given: the owner replies: keep feat-x’s version but change the title
examples.then: the card stays open with the change asked

title: A request is analysed only when the owner types /plumb clarify
statement: The request check runs only for typed /plumb clarify <words>: those words get the read-back, questions and the edit hold; an ordinary message runs no request check, raises no read-back or question card and closes no edit hold; the answer reader still reads a message for an answer while a card is waiting or the previous reply showed records, and nothing runs when neither is

examples.given: no card is waiting and the previous reply showed no records
examples.when: you type 'make the status line show the branch name'
examples.then: no model runs, no card is raised and edits are not held

examples.given: no card is waiting
examples.when: you type '/plumb clarify make the status line show the branch name'
examples.then: the words are checked: a read-back card is raised; edits are held while the check runs and until any question it asks is answered

examples.given: a question card is waiting
examples.when: you type 'go with the first option'
examples.then: the message is read as an answer to that card, and no request check runs

examples.given: the agent is asked to use a workflow for work you already asked for
examples.when: you type '/plumb clarify use a workflow to dispatch this update'
examples.then: no question about how to carry it out is raised; 'this update' is taken from your last message

title: One principle, asked once, settles the detailed cards and...
statement: When several open cards, or the gaps and conflicts of a request, hinge on one principle, plumb asks it once (one card naming what it would settle, or the request check's question for a commanded clarify) rather than each detail; once the owner's decision on it is confirmed, a background job settles each dependent card from the decision's words: withdrawn when answered, its link repinned when the meaning is kept, or a rewording proposed as an unconfirmed edit, each citing the decision, told in the one plumb line and undoable; a card the model cannot settle from the decision stays

examples.given: twenty stale-link cards hinge on what counts as the owner’s answer
examples.then: one principle card asks that question and lists the twenty cards it would settle; the twenty are not drawn

examples.given: the owner confirms the decision
examples.then: each of the twenty is withdrawn, repinned or gets a proposed rewording citing the decision, and the plumb line says how many of each

examples.given: a dependent card the model cannot settle from the decision’s words
examples.then: the card stays open and the plumb line says one could not be settled

examples.given: a settlement the owner disagrees with
examples.when: the owner says undo on it
examples.then: the card is back as it was and the repin or rewording is reverted

examples.given: the owner types /plumb clarify on a request whose five open gaps all hinge on whether cards or the question tool ask the owner
examples.then: one question asks that principle and names the five gaps it settles; the five are not asked

examples.given: a detailed gap that no principle settles
examples.then: it is asked on its own, as a specific question

title: The agent gets everything as text; the owner sees cards only
statement: The agent keeps receiving the session brief, the stale links, the untraced files and the warnings as text in its channel, with the panel up or not; the owner sees cards and the one plumb line only; the full/compact/off intent-card setting is retired

examples.given: the panel holds the session
examples.then: the agent still receives the brief as text

examples.given: a turn ends with stale links, untraced files and a warning
examples.then: the agent’s channel names them; the owner’s text is cards and one plumb line

examples.given: the full/compact/off setting is set
examples.then: the setting has no effect and plumb says once that it is retired

title: When no judge can be reached, plumb says so and blocks the step...
statement: When no judge can be reached (no key, timeout, API down), plumb says so once and the step that needed it (auto-approval, settling, triage, calibration, the stale check) waits until a judge is back; nothing is decided by rule; work that needs no judge goes on, and the request check keeps its build-anyway-or-wait card

examples.given: the judge’s key is missing
examples.then: one line says the judge is unreachable and the approval waits; nothing is approved by rule

examples.given: the judge’s key is missing
examples.when: the agent edits a file and the turn ends with no stale link
examples.then: work goes on; the turn is not held

examples.given: the judge is back
examples.then: it completes and the line is gone

title: Drift is checked for coverage before any card
statement: When code or tests linked to a requirement change and the requirement did not, plumb first checks the requirement is still covered: its linked tests pass and a model judges the meaning kept; then it repins and logs, with no card; a card is raised only when the requirement should change fundamentally (a confirmed example’s test weakened or deleted with no replacement, or the model says the statement or an example would now say something else) or when two confirmed records contradict

examples.given: src/plumb/commands.py is refactored under confirmed SR-003
examples.then: SR-003’s tests pass, the model judges the meaning kept, the link is repinned and logged; no card

examples.given: a confirmed example’s test is deleted with no replacement
examples.then: a card asks whether the requirement should change

examples.given: two confirmed records contradict each other
examples.then: one card asks which wins

examples.given: the model says the meaning changed in wording only
examples.then: a rewording is proposed as an unconfirmed edit and the link repinned; no card

title: Browser resolves Plumb issues through existing core semantics
statement: The local browser workspace lists source-session issues, full explanations, evidence and existing actions. Browser answers preserve exact-content approval and offer provenance without changing another surface's credentials, and remain distinct from verified repair completion.

examples.given: An issue and its current record are displayed
examples.when: The owner selects a supported answer
examples.then: Plumb records that action against exactly the displayed content and the browser shows its actual resulting state

examples.given: A displayed record changes before its answer
examples.then: The changed content is not approved and the browser explains the stale answer

examples.given: A Claude mod is already registered
examples.when: The browser opens and resolves an issue
examples.then: The mod registration is preserved and both surfaces retain valid distinct provenance

title: Issue explanations embed existing diagrams safely
statement: When an issue references a diagram-mod HTML or SVG artifact inside the project, the browser displays its extracted SVG in the explanation with text alternative and zoom controls. Missing, invalid, oversized or escaping artifacts are reported without disabling issue actions; diagram scripts never execute in the application DOM.

examples.given: A card references generated architecture HTML with toolbar icons
examples.then: The architecture SVG is displayed above its questions with readable labels

examples.given: A diagram is missing or its path escapes the project
examples.then: A clear fallback is shown and the owner's issue choices remain accessible

title: Browser follow-up reaches the matching agent turn truthfully
statement: Browser answers queue their follow-up for the source agent session; that session's next prompt hook delivers the context once without treating generated text as a typed owner approval. The browser distinguishes queued and delivered follow-ups and does not claim autonomous execution or successful repair.

examples.given: A browser answer queues a source-session follow-up
examples.then: The message remains queued for its intended session

examples.given: The intended session has a queued follow-up
examples.when: Its next turn hook emits context
examples.then: The follow-up is included once and delivery is shown separately from verification

title: Browser delivery includes independent interaction proof
statement: Independent subagents review and test the workspace's exposed buttons and navigation against a real local server with isolated fixtures, findings are fixed, and a browser demonstration plus screenshots and exact test outcomes are provided.

examples.given: The implemented workspace is served with isolated demo records
examples.then: Selections, actions, filters, history, tabs, diagrams, keyboard and narrow layouts are exercised and persisted action results checked

examples.given: Verification passes
examples.then: The browser is opened visibly and the user receives its URL, screenshots and measured results

title: The four queued browser integration defects are fixed and guarded
statement: Stale-link action state persists to its own store; an invalid button index leaves no false recovery handoff; a left-open turn-built card's fresh offer passes presentation validation; a custom combination requested for an unresolved conflict is not reported done. Each fix carries a regression test.

examples.given: A stale-link card is answered in the browser
examples.when: The server restarts and the card is drawn again
examples.then: The answer is still recorded and the card shows its settled state

examples.given: A press names a button index the offer does not have
examples.when: The next prompt hook runs for that session
examples.then: No recovery handoff is delivered; the press was refused and nothing durable remains

examples.given: A card built at turn time was left open
examples.then: Its fresh offer passes validation and its buttons work

examples.given: A conflict card has no resolution yet
examples.when: The owner asks for a custom combination
examples.then: The card stays open awaiting the combination and is not shown as done

title: Hook time limits are settings with defaults that survive a loaded...
statement: The watchdog's hard limit (hooks.hard_limit_s, default 30 s) and each hook's soft budget (hooks.budget_ms, default 20 s for session start, prompt and stop, 5 s after an edit) are settings read from .plumb/config.yaml, as are the covering-test budget of a turn (verify.turn_budget_s, default 60 s) and the judge's time inside a hook (judgment.hook_timeout_ms, default 5 s). The defaults sit above what a loaded machine needs and below the host's own hook timeouts (60 s, 120 s for the stop and async hooks), so a hook is cut only when it is truly stuck.

examples.given: a loaded machine where a hook takes 4 s to answer
examples.when: the hook runs with the default settings
examples.then: it is not cut and its check is not skipped

examples.given: a hook that never answers
examples.then: the watchdog cuts it with the budget notice, at the configured value

examples.given: config.yaml sets hooks.hard_limit_s and hooks.budget_ms
examples.then: the watchdog and the budgets use those values, and the defaults apply when unset

examples.given: the default hard limit plus the stop hook's grace
examples.when: the host hook timeouts are read from the plugin bundle
examples.then: every one of them is above that sum

title: The verdict judge is a cascade: JEV first, a judge model below its...
statement: A verdict on whether a record is supported by the owner’s words asks JEV first; when JEV’s probability is at or above the threshold calibrated on the owner’s labels with no false accept, the verdict is JEV’s and may feed auto-approval; below it, or with JEV not configured, the configured judge model (judge_model, haiku by default, sonnet allowed) gives the verdict used by cards and the tidy job, and a model verdict never approves an intent; it may confirm a requirement or a decision whose premise is the owner's verified words, as SR-191 says; with neither reachable the verdict waits and the step says so once

examples.given: JEV gives 0.9 for INT-003’s read-back and the calibrated threshold is 0.43
examples.then: the verdict is supported on JEV’s answer, the judge model is not called, and auto-approval may use it

examples.given: JEV gives 0.3 for SR-005’s example restatement
examples.then: the judge model judges it; its verdict is shown on the card and used by the tidy job; auto-approval does not use it

examples.given: judge_model is set to sonnet
examples.when: a verdict falls below JEV’s threshold
examples.then: Sonnet gives it, logged with the model’s name

examples.given: no JEV key and no judge model reachable
examples.then: the verdict waits, the step says so once, and nothing is decided by rule

title: JEV’s choice output is a configuration, off by default
statement: JEV’s question form is a setting (jev.output: yes_no by default, choice allowed); the choice form asks one choice over supported, beyond and contradicts and reads the probability of supported; calibration records which form it measured and a calibration from one form is never used for the other

examples.given: jev.output is unset
examples.then: it is asked yes/no as today

examples.given: jev.output is choice
examples.then: it is asked the three-way choice and the probability of supported is used; the log names the form

examples.given: a calibration measured with yes_no
examples.then: auto-approval does not run on the old calibration and jev status says a calibration for the choice form is needed

title: Browser workspace tests run only when asked for
statement: The default pytest run leaves tests/browser uncollected; naming the directory or passing --browser collects it.

examples.given: The whole suite is run with no path
examples.then: No test under tests/browser is collected

examples.given: The tests directory is named
examples.then: No test under tests/browser is collected

examples.given: The browser directory or one of its files is named
examples.then: Its tests are collected as before

examples.given: The flag --browser is passed with no path
examples.then: tests/browser is collected with the rest

examples.given: The whole suite is collected with --browser
examples.then: No import file mismatch error: the lane is a package like the other lanes

title: A judge job applies the verdicts it has; only the unanswered part...
statement: When the verdict cascade answers some records of a judge job and cannot answer the rest (the judge model unreachable, the diff too large, or an answer out of schema), the verdicts it has are applied and logged at once, the unanswered records stay in the job and wait, and one line says once per session window what waits and why; nothing is decided by rule for the unanswered part

examples.given: a judge job of five records, JEV clears two, and the judge model is unreachable
examples.then: the two verdicts are applied and logged as JEV's, the three others wait, and one line says they wait for the judge model

examples.given: the judge model answers out of schema for a job
examples.then: its records wait with the same waiting line, not an unresolved error

examples.given: the diff of a job is too large for the judge model
examples.then: its records wait with the waiting line that names the size

examples.given: every record of a job is answered
examples.then: nothing waits and no line is printed

title: Everything about verdicts follows judge_model
statement: The judge model setting (understand.judge_model, haiku by default) is the model for verdicts and for everything that measures or guards them: the evaluation run over the labelled set names and uses it, and the calibration fingerprint that suspends settling records it; understand.model stays the model that reads the owner's words (clarify, read, tidy)

examples.given: judge_model is sonnet and understand.model is haiku
examples.when: the evaluation run over the labelled set is made
examples.then: Sonnet judges and the run log names sonnet

examples.given: the same settings
examples.when: a logged calibration records its fingerprint
examples.then: the fingerprint names sonnet as the judge model

examples.given: the same settings
examples.when: a clarify or read job runs
examples.then: Haiku reads the owner's words, as understand.model says

examples.given: judge_model changes after a logged calibration
examples.then: settling is suspended until the evaluation set passes again, as for a prompt change

title: The clear part of a message is taken; only the unclear part is...
statement: When the owner's message does only part of what the reader looks for, the reader applies the clear part and leaves the rest: a side of a conflict picked in plain words (not the option's exact label) picks that option; a message that answers a card and adds a new request has the answer applied to the card and the new request read back; a part that is not clear stays open and is the only part asked about again

examples.given: a conflict card whose options are Keep this, Keep the other and Both
examples.when: the owner replies 'keep what main has'
examples.then: the reader names the option that side means and the conflict is settled on it

examples.given: a choice card with options 1, 2 and 3 shown in text
examples.when: the owner replies '2, and also make the pane resizable'
examples.then: the card is answered with option 2 and a read-back card is raised for the pane request only

examples.given: the same conflict card
examples.when: the owner replies 'hmm, either could work'
examples.then: the conflict stays open and nothing is recorded

examples.given: a message that answers a card and adds a request the reader cannot read
examples.then: the card is answered and the read-back for the request says what was unclear

title: a retired example keeps no test
statement: a retired example keeps no test: when a record is superseded, the tests that verified its examples are unlinked, and a test that then covers no live example is dropped; the superseding record keeps only the tests of what it states

examples.given: SR-002 supersedes SR-001 and SR-001/EX-1 is still verified by tests/test_a.py, which SR-002 does not verify
examples.then: it warns [retired-example] that SR-001/EX-1 is retired by SR-002 but still verified by tests/test_a.py and says to retire the test too: unlink it, and drop it when it covers nothing else; it never says to move the test to SR-002 or to keep SR-001

examples.given: the owner confirmed SR-001, SR-002 supersedes it, and SR-001#3 is the only test of SR-001 EX-2
examples.then: the link is removed: a superseded record's example is retired, so the only-test refusal does not protect it

examples.given: a test function whose sr markers name only superseded records and that no live record links to
examples.then: the test function is deleted (the whole file when nothing live remains); a test a live record still links to stays and only loses the retired id from its marker

examples.given: SR-001 has two tests verifying EX-1, tests/test_a.py and tests/test_b.py, and SR-002 supersedes it verifying neither
examples.then: both links are warned, one per link, not only the last one

examples.given: a commit with trailer SR-001 that unlinks tests/test_a.py from SR-001 and deletes the file
examples.when: plumb claims check runs over it
examples.then: tests/test_a.py is declared: a path a claimed record linked in the commit's parent counts, since a deleted file can no longer be linked

title: A worktree judges against the prompt log of its main checkout
statement: The hook logs the owner's prompts in the main checkout's .plumb/session/prompts.jsonl; a worktree of the same repository finds that log through git's common directory, so calibration, judge jobs, repins and captures run in a worktree see the owner's whole logged message exactly as the main checkout does

examples.given: an intent whose prompt digest names a message the hook logged in the main checkout
examples.when: plumb jev calibrate runs in a worktree of that repository
examples.then: the intent's premise is the whole message, as in the main checkout

examples.given: the same worktree
examples.then: the prompt is found without copying any line into the worktree

examples.given: a worktree with its own prompts.jsonl holding a line the main checkout lacks
examples.then: both logs are read and the latest entry of a digest wins

examples.given: a checkout that is not a worktree
examples.then: only its own log is read, as today

title: A judgment says when it had only the quote
statement: When a record's premise is its quote alone because no logged prompt holds it, every judgment and verdict logged for it carries premise: quote-only with the reason (no prompt named, prompt not found, quote not verbatim), a calibration's log entry and plumb jev status report how many items were judged on the quote alone, and nothing is decided by rule from it

examples.given: an intent with no prompt field
examples.then: the judgment entry says premise: quote-only, reason: no prompt named

examples.given: 25 of 46 labelled intents have a quote-only premise
examples.then: the calibration entry records quote_only: 25 of 46 and plumb jev status prints that line

examples.given: a record whose premise is the whole message
examples.then: the entry carries no quote-only mark

title: The judge model's supported verdict confirms requirements and...
statement: When the verdict cascade's judge model finds a proposed requirement or decision supported, that record's premise is the owner's verified words (not the quote alone), and the owner's auto-approve switch is on with the verdict's confidence at or above the owner's min_probability and min_confidence, the record is confirmed by: auto-model with the verdict's confidence and the model's name, the end-of-turn summary lists each such confirmation once in the owner's words, and one Undo press or the owner's word revokes it; below those settings, or with the switch off, the verdict is logged and confirms nothing, and reading the log refuses such an approval as it refuses an auto-jev one; an intent is never confirmed by a model verdict, and JEV's verdict confirms as SR-113 says

examples.given: the owner's auto-approve is on at min_probability 0.7 and min_confidence medium, SR-185 is proposed, its premise is the owner's logged message, and the judge model says supported at 0.8
examples.when: the judge job applies its verdicts
examples.then: SR-185 is confirmed by: auto-model (haiku, 0.8) and the next summary lists it

examples.given: INT-067 is proposed and the judge model says supported
examples.then: INT-067 stays proposed; the summary says it waits for the owner's words

examples.given: a decision whose premise is the quote alone
examples.then: it stays proposed and the verdict is logged quote-only

examples.given: SR-185 was confirmed by the model
examples.when: the owner presses Undo on the summary line or says to undo it
examples.then: the confirmation is revoked and SR-185 is proposed again, counted as a 'no' label

examples.given: the owner's auto-approve is on with min_confidence high, and the judge model says SR-185 is supported at 0.6
examples.when: the judge job applies its verdicts
examples.then: the verdict is logged and SR-185 stays proposed

examples.given: a worker wrote a by: auto-model approval at confidence 0.6 while the owner's min_probability is 0.9
examples.then: the approval is refused and SR-185 is proposed

title: A background plumb process opens no console window on Windows
statement: On Windows, every background process plumb starts (the understand worker, the background test map) is created with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and a new process group and never with DETACHED_PROCESS, so neither it nor any git, pytest or model command it runs opens a console window; it still outlives the process that started it; on other systems the launch starts its own session as before

examples.given: a Windows machine
examples.when: the stop hook starts the understand worker
examples.then: no console window appears for the worker nor for the commands it runs

examples.given: a Windows machine
examples.then: no console window appears for it nor for its git and pytest calls

examples.given: the hook that started a background process has exited
examples.then: it keeps running to the end of its work

examples.given: macOS or Linux
examples.then: it starts in its own session, as before

title: /plumb intent opens the intent loop on command
statement: Typing /plumb intent <words> opens one interactive loop for that intent: the clarifier asks every blocking question through the question tool, checks each answer against the confirmed records as it goes and asks about any contradiction or extension it finds, writes the intent candidates, and passes them through one judge gate with a fix loop until only low findings remain. An ordinary message opens no loop.

examples.given: no loop is open
examples.when: the owner types /plumb intent add multiply next to add
examples.then: the blocking questions come through the question tool, as many as there are gaps, and no record is written until the intent is clear

examples.given: an intent candidate contradicts a confirmed requirement's example
examples.then: the contradiction is put to the owner as a question before the candidate is written, naming the requirement

examples.given: the judge gate finds a high finding on a candidate
examples.then: the candidate is fixed and judged again, and the loop ends only when every finding left is low

examples.given: no loop is open
examples.when: the owner types make the status line show the branch name
examples.then: no loop opens and no model runs

title: A stage of the intent loop runs only on the passed gate of the...
statement: Each stage of the intent loop (clarify and integrate, update records and plans, build and prove) records its outcome in the intent's session state, and the command of the next stage refuses to run until the previous stage's review gate passed; a workflow phase carries each gate, and the owner can see which gate is open.

examples.given: clarification has not passed its judge gate
examples.when: the update stage is asked to run
examples.then: it refuses and names the gate that has not passed

examples.given: the judge gate passed with only low findings
examples.then: it proceeds and records that it ran on that gate

examples.given: the build stage finished
examples.when: the proof the owner stated has not been shown
examples.then: the intent is not called done

examples.given: stage B applies the record updates and a new requirement supersedes one whose tests still cover the behaviour
examples.then: plumb relink moves each link to the new requirement with a note, plumb repin --after-tests pins it once the linked tests pass, and a test of a retired example is unlinked with plumb unlink --note and deleted in the same commit

examples.given: stage C edits code that a confirmed requirement's link pins
examples.when: the edit hook reports the link stale
examples.then: the agent repins it after the linked tests pass, relinks it when the code moved, or cards it when the meaning changed, before the turn ends; the merge boundary holds any link problem left

title: A requirement is one durable behaviour; the record set is version 2
statement: Each requirement states one durable, observable behaviour of plumb with examples and a proof, under a feature; a fix of a behaviour a requirement already states is recorded under that requirement (its commit trailer, or an NC when it was broken), never as a new requirement; an intent is one per principle. The version 2 set replaces the current one in place: every older record a version 2 record replaces is retired with a supersedes trail, its links stop counting, and one repin pass relinks the tests.

examples.given: SR-005, SR-112 and SR-168 each state the confirmation rule
examples.then: one requirement states the rule and the three are retired, superseded by it, with their tests relinked to it

examples.given: a behaviour a requirement states is broken (a background process opens a console window)
examples.then: the commit claims that requirement and no new requirement appears

examples.given: the owner states a new principle
examples.then: one intent records it, and the requirements it changes are named at capture

title: Outside the loop, the edit gate closes only on an intent change
statement: Outside the intent loop the hooks keep grounding: the brief, the relevant records, drift at the edit, covering tests at the end of the turn. The edit gate closes when a request or an edit would contradict or extend what a confirmed record covers and no intent loop has run for that request; it opens when the loop reaches a clear intent for it, or when the owner releases it. A request that changes nothing a confirmed record covers never closes the gate.

examples.given: SR-001 is confirmed with the example add(1, 2) returns 3 and no loop ran
examples.when: the prompt says make add subtract
examples.then: the edit gate closes and names SR-001 and its example

examples.given: the same prompt after /plumb intent reached a clear intent for it
examples.then: the edit proceeds

examples.given: no confirmed record covers the status line's colour
examples.when: the prompt asks to change that colour
examples.then: the gate stays open and no model runs

title: The proof of an intent is stated by the owner in the loop and...
statement: During the loop the owner states how they will see the intent working; the proof is recorded on the intent's requirements as a plan whose kind is live-session, hook, command or other; the plan of updates includes the code the proof needs; the build is called done only once the proof has been shown and its evidence recorded.

examples.given: the owner states the proof as 'I open the panel and see the card'
examples.then: the plan carries that proof as a live-session proof and the code it needs

examples.given: the build is finished and the proof was not shown
examples.when: the agent calls the intent done
examples.then: plumb says the proof is missing and the intent stays open

title: Logs are two JSONL streams
question: How are the append-only logs stored?
chosen: Two hash-chained JSONL streams, .plumb/log/events.jsonl and evidence.jsonl, with merge=union in git.
alternatives: One JSON file per log entry under .plumb/log/<kind>/ (concept 4.7).

title: Guard by deny rules and the session marker
question: How is plumb approve kept from the agent?
chosen: Declarative permissions.deny rules in .claude/settings.json plus the CLI session-marker check.
alternatives: A PreToolUse hook on every shell call (concept 4.6).

title: Relayed approvals use plumb relay
question: Which command records an approval the agent relays?
chosen: A separate plumb relay command; plumb approve is the owner's only.
alternatives: plumb approve --prompt --quote (concept 4.6).

title: Prompt digests committed only when cited
question: Where are prompt digests kept?
chosen: The prompt hook writes {digest, session, at, text} to gitignored session state; plumb relay copies the cited {digest, session, at} into events.jsonl before the approval.
alternatives: The prompt hook writes every prompt digest to a committed log (concept 4.6, 6.2).

title: Per-run test evidence in the committed log
question: Where does per-turn test evidence live?
chosen: plumb tests run appends one compact entry per run to the committed .plumb/log/evidence.jsonl; the cache keeps only a derived reuse index.
alternatives: Evidence in the cache until the merge boundary (concept 4.1, 7.3).

title: Covering tests run in the agent's turn
question: Who runs the covering tests each turn?
chosen: The stop hook blocks once per turn asking the agent to run plumb tests run --changed; the hook never runs pytest itself.
alternatives: The stop hook runs the tests itself.
The stop hook asks for plumb verify (concept 6.4).

title: Sub-project 1 command names
question: What are the commands called?
chosen: plumb validate, plumb tests map, plumb tests run, plumb hooks install, plumb statusline; the concept names stay as aliases.
alternatives: plumb check, plumb map, plumb verify, plumb install claude-code, plumb status --line.

title: Session brief of about 30 lines
question: How long is the session brief?
chosen: About 30 lines, hard cap 40.
alternatives: At most about 60 lines (concept 6.1).

title: Turn budget of 15 seconds
question: How long may per-turn tests run?
chosen: verify.turn_budget_s 15 s, hard limit 1.5x.
alternatives: 30 s, hard limit 2x (concept 7.2).

title: Regression keyed by test node, exactly as R3
question: When is a failing test a regression?
chosen: An existing node with an earlier passed or flaky test-run entry that now fails is a regression even if its source changed; only a new test that starts red is exempt.
alternatives: Exempt a test whose source changed since its pass.

title: The minimal importer imports everything as proposed
question: What approval state do imported records get?
chosen: Every imported record is proposed; by: import approvals wait for the full importer.
alternatives: Records with an upstream approval get by: import (concept 10).

title: Links live in their source record
question: Where are links stored?
chosen: In the source record's links list; Link and LinkState are first-class types and plumb link a command.
alternatives: One file per link.

title: Build order: core first, then bootstrap, then lanes
question: In what order is sub-project 1 built?
chosen: The CORE lane alone first, then the dogfood bootstrap, then VERIFY, HOST and BRIDGE in parallel on top of it, each part set up in plumb's repository as it lands.
alternatives: Slice 1a built strictly in the listed order (concept 11).

title: Build order: a contracts phase alone, then five lanes in parallel
question: How are sub-projects 2 to 5 and the importer completion built?
chosen: The coordinator first writes every cross-lane signature, data class, route, config key and stub in a contracts phase on main; then CAPTURE, MERGE, HOSTS, PRESENT and IMPORT run in parallel on disjoint files.
alternatives: The sub-projects one after another, in roadmap order.
Five lanes with no contracts phase, each defining what it needs.

title: The importer completion shares FEAT-004 with the other hosts
question: Which feature holds the importer completion's requirements, given four new features?
chosen: FEAT-004, beside the Codex, Pi, Hermes and MCP adapters, as the other way plumb reaches an existing environment; the importer is its own lane (IMPORT).
alternatives: A sixth feature for the importer.
FEAT-001, beside the minimal importer SR-023.

title: Auto-approval is on only through the owner's logged config event
question: What turns auto-approval on, given that the agent can edit .plumb/config.yaml?
chosen: Only the owner turns auto-approval on or off: plumb config auto-approve in the owner's terminal, a /plumb auto-approve on|off the owner typed as a whole message in Claude Code (plumb saw it arrive through the prompt hook), or the SP7 settings button; each is logged as the owner's config event. config.yaml is a mirror; a yaml saying on without that event is off with a validate warning. The agent can never write the event.
alternatives: The config.yaml key alone.
A deny rule on editing config.yaml.
The owner's terminal only.

title: The grouped one-line confirmation names up to 5 records, then +N...
question: How can one "ok" confirm a triage group whose records were not each shown in full?
chosen: TOP 5 + MORE (owner, R13 Q2): the one-line offer names up to about 5 records by title, then "+N more (see plumb triage)"; the stated set holds the whole group with its hashes; the owner's ok approves exactly that pinned list (plumb relay --group, agent-relayed, after the R2 quote checks), which plumb triage shows in full.
alternatives: Name every record of the group by ID in the offer line.
Show every record of the group in full before an ok counts.
Only plumb triage --approve in the owner's terminal.

title: Calibration needs mixed evidence: 20 owner decisions and 5 'no'...
question: When does a calibration pass for auto-approval?
chosen: MIXED EVIDENCE (owner, R13 Q1): per record kind, at least 20 of the owner's past decisions and at least 5 'no' examples, up to half of which may be generated variations (a will flipped to won't, a flipped result, a changed number); JEV must wrongly accept none of them, every generated one included, and accept at least half of the owner's confirmed records; the real/generated split is shown in plumb jev status and in the calibration event.
alternatives: Only real 'no' examples, however few a project has.
A fixed 0.9 threshold without measurement.
Precision of at least 0.95 with any number of items.

title: The R8 commands live in sub-project 2; their owner-facing views in sub-project 5
question: Where do the R8 commands belong, given they are both capture data and presentation?
chosen: Sub-project 2 (CAPTURE) builds plumb triage, plumb config and plumb jev and the data behind them; sub-project 5 (PRESENT) shows them to the owner: the triage offer line, /plumb review and /plumb confirm, and "confirmed by you" or "by JEV" in the cards.
alternatives: Everything R8 in sub-project 5.

title: An intent conflict lives inside the conflicted record
question: Where is an intent conflict recorded?
chosen: inside the conflicted record file, as a conflict block with an IC-### ID
alternatives: a separate .plumb/conflicts/IC-###.md record file

title: An intent conflict does not stop git's merge; the boundary holds it
question: What happens to git's merge when a record has an intent conflict?
chosen: the merge completes with the record unconfirmed and carrying the conflict; plumb check --merge and the optional pre-merge-commit hook hold it until the owner chooses
alternatives: the driver stops git's merge until the owner chooses

title: On an ID collision the branch merged into keeps its IDs
question: Which record keeps the ID when two clones created the same one?
chosen: the first parent (the branch merged into) keeps its IDs and the incoming record is renumbered
alternatives: the older record keeps its ID
the owner picks each time

title: The plugin carries a ready-built plumb and sets up a private copy of its tools
question: How does the plugin get its own plumb, independent of the project it runs in?
chosen: The plugin carries a ready-built copy of plumb, checked to match plumb's source; on first use it sets up a private copy of plumb's tools per user and per plugin version; git's checks call one stable plumb launcher in the user's own folder.
alternatives: Make the whole plumb repository the plugin and run plumb straight from its source.
Download plumb from its repository when the plugin is installed.

title: plumb's background checks keep doing the work; the in-app panel shows it
question: What does the in-app panel do, and what stays with plumb's background checks?
chosen: The background checks keep noting the owner's messages, guarding against the agent confirming for the owner, tracking edits and running each turn's checks; the panel draws the band, the panel view, the summary line and the buttons from what they recorded, holds the session background, and the background checks stay quiet toward the owner while the panel is active.
alternatives: The panel replaces the background checks.
The panel only draws, and the background checks still print everything.

title: A button press is proven by a secret only the panel holds
question: How does plumb know a Confirm press came from the owner and not the agent?
chosen: At session start the panel makes a random secret and keeps it in memory; plumb learns only enough to recognise it, never the secret itself; the first panel to register in a session wins; a press sends the secret with what was pressed; the agent's shell is not allowed to run the button steps.
alternatives: Ask the owner again in a terminal.
Trust any call that says it came from a button.

title: How should calibration treat a read-back the owner rejected?
question: How should calibration treat a read-back the owner rejected?
chosen: Recapture always; the old version counts as a calibration no only when the owner says it misread their words; an intent change gets no label
alternatives: Recapture always and never label the old version
Every rejection counts as a calibration no (SR-096 as written)

title: Which language model reads the owner's message to extract...
question: Which language model reads the owner's message to extract approvals and rejections?
chosen: A small model run through the host's own way of dispatching work to an agent (Claude Code: Haiku via claude -p with a plumb agent and no tools; Hermes: a delegated child session), or OpenRouter when configured; never the coding agent; an unreachable model is an error, with no fallback
alternatives: The coding agent itself (Claude in the session) reads the message and reports what the owner approved
JEV, the judgment model plumb already uses
A small model through OpenRouter only

title: Where does the progress of a long execution show?
question: Where does the progress of a long execution show?
chosen: Both: a bar in the terminal, plain lines in a non-terminal shell, and the same message in the Claude Code status line (since the owner watches the agent, not the shell)
alternatives: Only in the terminal or shell where the command runs

title: How is the ~150-record proposed backlog worked through?
question: How is the ~150-record proposed backlog worked through?
chosen: Judge the whole backlog in one background pass, then show one card per feature (e.g. these 18 about the merge check would be settled; right?)
alternatives: Batches of about five, worked through gradually (the owner's answer of 9 Oct, superseded on 10 Oct)

title: Who switches settling on once calibration passes?
question: Who switches settling on once calibration passes?
chosen: Settling switches on by itself, once calibrated, for records the agent derives (requirements and their examples); the owner still switches it on for intents and still answers decisions that matter
alternatives: The owner switches it on for every kind (the owner's answer of 9 Oct, narrowed on 10 Oct)

title: In what order does work go now?
question: In what order does work go now?
chosen: Re-align SP7 with SP8 and build it in parallel with the everyday loop (confirming and verifying its requirements), in separate worktrees
alternatives: Freeze SP6 and SP7 feature work; first make the hooks fast, then build SP8, then get the requirements of the everyday loop confirmed and verified; then resume SP7

title: After 'Ask for a change', the owner's words go to the message box
question: After 'Ask for a change', where do the owner's words go?
chosen: The click puts the cursor in the message box with "Change to '<topic>': " written; what the owner types is read against that card. If the panel cannot prefill the box, the agent asks one question in its next reply.
alternatives: The agent always asks in its next reply.

title: 'No' is a button where the card suggests it
question: Is 'No' (drop it, wait) a button too?
chosen: Yes, wherever the card suggests it (a trial or backlog no, 'drop it' on a card beyond the owner's words, 'wait' on a failed check), beside Ask for a change and Leave open; elsewhere only Confirm, Ask for a change and Leave open.
alternatives: Only the three buttons the owner named.

title: 'Leave open' stops a card repeating at turn end until its record...
question: How long does 'Leave open' last?
chosen: Until the owner presses Leave open, the card shows at the end of every turn. After the press it no longer repeats at turn end until its record changes; it stays listed under what awaits the owner in the band and the pane, and /plumb shows it again on request. It never confirms, settles or rejects anything.
alternatives: The card keeps showing at every turn end, or less often, even after Leave open.

title: When is the Claude Code mod (the card panel with buttons) built?
question: When is the Claude Code mod (the card panel with buttons) built?
chosen: Now, in parallel with slice 3: slice 4 (the press, Python side) and slice 6 (the plugin) first, then slice 7 (the mod: band and card panel) as soon as slice 3's cards land
alternatives: After slices 3 to 6 in order, as planned

title: How should /plumb stop meaning two things?
question: How should /plumb stop meaning two things?
chosen: rename the grounding skill to plumb-records
alternatives: keep the name and set user-invocable: false

title: Should a missing proof block the merge?
question: Should a missing proof block the merge?
chosen: plumb names it; the owner decides
alternatives: block the merge until a proof is shown

title: Keep calibrating the judge with trial cards, or rely on context...
question: Keep calibrating the judge with trial cards, or rely on context settling and typed corrections alone?
chosen: keep trial cards, in the read-back shape, at most three open
alternatives: drop trial cards; calibrate from typed corrections and context settling only

title: Does a question the agent can recommend on block the build?
question: Does a question the agent can recommend on block the build?
chosen: no: it becomes a flippable assumption; only a question with no recommendation and a costly wrong pick blocks
alternatives: every gap blocks until answered

title: Keep both settling by context and the word-reading judge, as...
question: Keep both settling by context and the word-reading judge, as INT-032 asked, or one?
chosen: one: the judge that reads the owner's words, calibrated by trial cards; settling by context is removed
alternatives: keep both, as INT-032 said

title: Which diagram skill?
question: Which diagram skill?
chosen: architecture-diagram (Cocoon AI): instructions and a template, the agent writes the SVG
alternatives: archify, its fork with a Node renderer, schemas and a browser gate

title: Where does the mod live?
question: Where does the mod live?
chosen: its own repository, C:/coding/diagram-mod, used beside plumb
alternatives: a second plugin inside plumb's repository

title: SR-128 The request check reads the request with its conversation:...

chosen: fix/plugin-review's version
alternatives: main's version
both, combined

title: Where does the card's drawing code come from?
question: Where does the card's drawing code come from?
chosen: the diagram mod exposes its parser and renderer on $ as a noun; plumb's plugin depends on it and calls it
alternatives: copy svg.ts and grid.ts into plumb's plugin
plumb's card opens the diagram mod's pane next to the card pane

title: When a link is removed, what happens to the numbers of the links...
question: When a link is removed, what happens to the numbers of the links after it?
chosen: they move down by one, and the command prints every new number
alternatives: leave a removed placeholder so numbers never change

title: Who may remove or move a link?
question: Who may remove or move a link?
chosen: the agent, like plumb link, with a required note logged; removing a confirmed example's only live test is refused
alternatives: only the owner from their own terminal

title: Fold the judge's doubts into the read-back
question: How should the judge's 'goes beyond' and 'contradicts' findings reach the owner?
chosen: As one line on the request's read-back card
alternatives: keep a card per record, reworded in the second person
show them only in plumb review

title: Where should the owner answer a merge conflict?
question: Where should the owner answer a merge conflict?
chosen: On its card, or through the agent in chat: a model reads the owner's words and the choice applies only when they clearly pick one version
alternatives: Only on its card
Decide later

title: The first browser product is an issue-resolution workspace
question: What should the browser become first?
chosen: Issue-resolution workspace: understand issues, answer them, and follow repairs; agents may run elsewhere.
alternatives: Agent workspace with start, steer, pause and resume controls.
Project control centre coordinating multiple repositories, agents and people.

title: One project and Plumb issue resolution; agent integration remains open
question: What scope should the first browser workspace cover?
chosen: Resolve each kind of Plumb issue within one project. Leave general team coordination and assignments to the underlying harness. Whether to include an issue-resolution coding agent initially is reopened for design exploration.
alternatives: Aggregate issues across projects.
Embed an agent workspace and team assignment system immediately.

title: Base browser resolution behaviour on existing cards and mods
question: What behaviour should browser issue resolution follow?
chosen: Use existing Plumb card and mod behaviour as the baseline, including the connection to agent follow-up.
alternatives: Create a separate issue-resolution agent with a new autonomy model.
Build an approval-only browser disconnected from agent follow-up.

title: Should Sonnet replace JEV/Haiku in the judging runs?
question: Should Sonnet replace JEV/Haiku in the judging runs?
chosen: Add Sonnet as an option: JEV/Haiku stay as they are and a run can choose Sonnet
alternatives: Everywhere they run
Only that one run

title: Should JEV's choice output be supported?
question: Should JEV's choice output be supported?
chosen: Keep supporting JEV's choice output as a configuration, though an earlier evaluation showed it judged worse than yes/no
alternatives: Drop choice output

title: What counts as the owner’s answer to plumb?
question: What counts as the owner’s answer to plumb?
chosen: Only what plumb saw itself: a card press, a typed /plumb command, or the owner’s own message read by plumb against the question it answers; the agent never carries the answer
alternatives: Also words the agent relays, checked by a model
Anything the agent reports the owner agreed to

title: Commands replace the automatic request check
question: Should the commands replace the automatic per-turn intent check, or sit beside it?
chosen: Replace it: intent is analysed only when a command is used, and ordinary messages run no model
alternatives: Sit beside it: the model still reads ordinary messages, and commands only force or skip analysis for a turn

title: Now that the panel shows cards, what does the agent get and what...
question: Now that the panel shows cards, what does the agent get and what does the owner see?
chosen: The agent keeps getting everything as text (brief, stale links, untraced files, warnings); the owner sees cards only; the full/compact/off setting is retired
alternatives: The agent is told only what blocks it
Keep the old text for both, with the full/compact/off setting

title: When no judge can be reached, what does plumb do?
question: When no judge can be reached, what does plumb do?
chosen: Say so once and block the step that needs the judge; work that needs no judge goes on; nothing is decided by rule
alternatives: Say so once and skip, never block
Fall back to simple rules

title: When code or tests linked to a confirmed requirement change, when...
question: When code or tests linked to a confirmed requirement change, when is the owner asked?
chosen: Never by default: plumb checks the requirement is still covered and repins; a card only when the requirement should change fundamentally or two confirmed records contradict
alternatives: A card on every change to what the owner confirmed
A card only on contradictions, everything else settled by the agent

title: Where does the remaining work continue?
question: Where does the remaining work continue?
chosen: On feat/browser-issue-workspace in its existing worktree, committed per task as the plan set out

title: How long may a hook run before the watchdog cuts it?
question: How long may a hook run before the watchdog cuts it?
chosen: A configurable hooks.hard_limit_s, defaulting to 6 s, with soft budgets about 4 s; the 2-second rule gives way.
alternatives: Keep the fixed 1.9 s limit.
Remove the watchdog.

title: Which judge decides whether a record is supported, and which may...
question: Which judge decides whether a record is supported, and which may auto-approve?
chosen: A cascade: JEV above its zero-false-accept threshold decides and may auto-approve; below it the judge model decides for cards and tidying, and its verdict may confirm a requirement or decision (never an intent) only under the owner's auto-approve settings, as DEC-073 and SR-191 say
alternatives: One judge model for everything
JEV alone

title: What does a passing test on a retired example mean?
question: What does a passing test on a retired example mean?
chosen: Retired means gone: the test is unmarked or deleted along with the example; the superseding record keeps only what it states.
alternatives: The behaviour lives on: the test's marker, or the example itself, moves to the superseding record.

title: What is the rule for links left stale from before the drift gate?
question: What is the rule for links left stale from before the drift gate?
chosen: One baseline pass in one commit: every stale link whose covering tests pass is repinned; links with no test are judged on meaning and those judged changed are carded, grouped by record. The gate holds from there.
alternatives: Every stale link goes through the meaning judge; each changed verdict becomes a card grouped by record.

title: Which edit to a confirmed record must the owner reconfirm?
question: Which edit to a confirmed record must the owner reconfirm?
chosen: Every edit, asked once per principle (e.g. read-back on command) with the derived records listed, never one card per record.
alternatives: Only an edit that changes an example's then-clause; a rewording keeps the record confirmed.

title: When a judge job can only be partly answered, what happens?
question: When a judge job can only be partly answered, what happens?
chosen: Apply what is answered: existing verdicts are applied at once; only the rest waits, with one line saying what waits and why.
alternatives: The whole job waits until every record has a verdict.

title: Which setting does everything about verdicts follow?
question: Which setting does everything about verdicts follow?

alternatives: One model for all jobs: drop judge_model.

title: How is a message taken that does only part of what the reader...
question: How is a message taken that does only part of what the reader looks for?
chosen: Take what is clear: the clear part is applied, the rest is read back or left open, and only the unclear part is asked about.
alternatives: Take nothing and ask the whole question again.

question: May a judge model's verdict confirm a record?
